Two week ago I have (for the first time ever)  played the original Half-Life. For the people who don't know, Half-Life was the first game that Valve has ever released. The game started the success of Valve that resulted in many game classics and Steam (on which you are now reading this review).
Half-Life itself is a first person shooter. The big difference between Half-Life and other first person shooters is that instead of just shooting, it also has exploration parts through puzzles and platforming. What I really liked is that nothing in the game takes the control away from the player. You go through the entire game and choose what to do by yourself at any given moment. The game doesn't have cutscenes and the story is experienced through gameplay and dialogue. But you can also just walk past all the characters in the story and just continue. I really appreciated this, because if you die you don't have to listen to what you already know. That makes following the story optional, even though there is only a little bit of story given which is basically just: You work at a research lab and everything went wrong. Try to escape. Many parts of the story are mysteries  you just have to figure out by yourself throughout the game. I only got annoyed once due to a scientist explaining what was already shown to me through gameplay.
The first experience of playing Half-Life felt a little bit boring. The loading for areas was really annoying, and I thought the game didn't look all that well. After a while though I got into it, and I didn't stop. Thanks to this game, I have a new insane record of non-stop playing without leaving my chair for 13.2 hours, until I completed the game. I guess that also has to do with the fact that it was my first day of my vacation, and hadn't played a game for a long while.
What makes the game so much fun is that you feel so free because nothing is told and you have to figure everything out by yourself through gameplay, which is really satisfying. I never really got stuck for a long while, because everything you find in a room has a reason to be there.
The shooting is also fun and gets even more fun over time. The only problem I had, which might just be a personal issue, is that I think the weapons were not very well balanced. For instance, I wish the shotgun did more damage to make it an instant-kill up close. What I also liked is that in the game there are enough exploration parts and different roads to take, which resulted in me knowing  I haven't seen everything yet.
After I finished Half-Life I found out that Valve has updated this original version of Half-Life with better textures, sound and other stuff so that explains why it is easier to look at the old things after a while and be amazed by what Half-Life really is.
In conclusion, I can say that I still recommend playing this updated version of the original Half-Life. What makes Half-Life special is the variety of shooting, puzzle solving and platforming and the lack of hand holding throughout the story and the entire game itself. Playing through Half-Life can make you think about whether we took more steps backwards than forwards with the games nowadays.

This game suffered bugs in it's early release, but for the most part these have been fixed. It demands alot, but if your computer can handle it it is a well-detailed, decently functioning game. It has some interesting new side activities (murder mysteries for instance, though these can occasionally be less than satisfying).
It also fixed a lot that was wrong with the previous titles. Arno is the first Assassin who can free run down buildings, a much needed development. He can also crouch and hide behind objects (properly). These are skills you might have expected to appear in the franchise earlier on.
My complaints though, are not technical. The characters in this game failed to intruigue and excite me like they had in it's predecessor 'Blag Flag'. To be quite honest, I couldn't care less about Arno. Not to mention the landscape is bleak and repetitive. The story is mediocre, and at times difficult to keep up with.
I have not played the multiplayer feature very much, and don't feel able to comment on that.
If you're committed to the franchise. I would recommend this game. But I would certainly rate it one of the poorer titles in the Assassin's Creed collection

Like many others, I bought this game expecting a re-released version of the original with some graphics updates and without the hassle of getting an old copy to run on modern hardware. This is not that game.
What we have instead is a stripped-down version with less cars, fewer stages and fewer set-up/repair options which was previously released for mobile devices. Between purchase and writing this review the store description has been updated to reflect this, but it still leaves a faint glimmer of hope that this might be something better. Don't be under any illusions  - you're paying to play the mobile version with better controls on a bigger screen.
In fairness to Codemasters, this is at least a competent driving game. The cars handle at least as well as in the original, with noticeable changes between surfaces. Car damage does affect performance, but the scaled-back repair interface takes away most of the decisions in choosing what to fix between stages. There are only four cars available to drive (three of which must be unlocked by completing events), but they recreated as well as possible in the engine.
Ultimately though, I can't recommend this. It may only be £4.99, but that still feels expensive for a cut-down version of a ten-year-old game. You would be better-off spending your money on a copy of the original on ebay and taking the time to get it working

Going to do this one a lttle different than how I usually do it. I wish I could've been a little more Cynical but honestly I couldn't think of any faults that I ran into while playing Bastion.
First I would just like to say, the last Two Hours of this Game were probably the best Moments I've ever had in a Video Game.

The Combat.-
Typical Diablo-Styled Action RPG Combat except you really only get Three Attacks and no Hotkeys. You click M1 to Attack with your Primary, M2 for Secondary, and M3/Q for your Special. While this type of Combat may seem a little primitive compared to Diablo's, the amount of Weapons and Specials you get sure makes up for it. You also have the ability to Dodgeroll with Space and Block/Deflect enemy attacks with Shift. I found the Combat quite enjoyable overall.
The Music-
Beautiful, absolutely beautiful. The sound design is phenomenal. I honestly have no complaints.
The Story-
Short but Amazing. I'm not going to give anything away, though I suspect most of you already know the Story of the Game. I just wanted to say that while the Story was amazing, it would only be half as good without the Narrator. Whoever did the Voice for the Narrator deserves a Cookie.
Closing Thoughts-
So, yeah. Those are my thoughts on the Game. I recomend you get it if you're looking for a Good Story Game, A Game with a Good Soundtrack, a Game with Fun Diablo-Styled Combat, or just a Good Game in General.

Strangely addictive, punchy little game. The tutorial gets right to the point and explains the basics to you, then just dumps you into the world, which is nice. I most definately reccomend this game, especially with friends, because it has a great inclusion of co-op and trading with other players that is not only functional, but COMPLETELY optional. Because of it's instant Nexus button, this is a great game for hopping on with friends on a whim in those inbetween moments and getting back off. It's not hard set a time and meet it because there's no penalty for nexusing and there are no cut scenes. But you won't want to. It's the kind of game that you can pour hours into exploring classes and, should you accidentally die, there's not much lost. It's a good game for exploring a play style without having to be careful. If you're impatient, you're allowed to jump right in and be messy; it never discourages you to explore, try things or take risks. Limited inventory and storage space presents a huge challenge that I enjoy because it makes you weigh the risks of carrying nice items, so that when you do lose them, you'll be sorry for it. But maybe only a day. Pets are fun if you like surprizes, but they're also useful, especially heath pets. And this is one game that you don't want to wiki if you don't have to. Half the fun is discovering new armor, rings, weapons and pets. But my reccommendation comes with a single warning: disable in game purchase hot keys. I used up a lot of hand out cash at the onset because of that dang "buy potions" key that was next to WASD. After I disabled in-game purchases, and never had any problems apart from the initial incident. If I could say one thing that is inexcusable, it's this: when the game opens it has a big banner for today's "deals". I hate these. If you have to have this, please allow me to disable it when I disable in-game purchases, because otherwise, it's just in my way.

Overall, an excellent third-person sneaker / assassin game.
PROS
An interesting twist on the "deadly assassin" theme, where your character (Shadwen) finds herself looking out for (and growing attached to) a little orphan girl while on the job. Provides a unique emotional twist; I never enjoy gratuitous violence in games, but I find myself feeling guilty on another level. You have a constant choice to either hide your brutal handiwork from Lily, or not. So far I've been careful to hide the bodies.
The grappling hook and the ability to reverse time are also very cool, and allow for some fun parkour stunts.
Beautifully rendered and highly atmospheric setting.
CONS
- The grappling hook can be a bit wonky at times.
- I often I wish I could speed up Reverse Time to more than 1x.
- So far, the character development and dialog between Lily and Shadwen feels a bit simplistic & two-dimensional. That's during the cutscenes; there's basically no direct interaction between them during gameplay.
- Being seen AT ALL, or letting a guard spot a body (even if the kill was indirect, such as a falling barrel) results in an immediate game over. Not a huge deal, since you can just reverse time, but it'd be interesting if there was a small window to "get out of dodge" -- kill the alerted guard then run and hide, for instance.
- Lily is actually invisible to the guards! This adds a certain futility to all the work you do trying to get her through the area "safely". I suspect the reason for this is that Lily's AI can't always determine accurately when its safe to progress to the next hiding place; it would be incredibly frustrating to watch the AI stupidly dart out right in front of a guard only to get caught, or worse, to have it hunker down indefinitely when you knew it was all clear. But maybe instead of being invisible, she could get caught, and then you'd have to rescue her before leaving the area?

Two week ago I have (for the first time ever)  played the original Half-Life. For the people who don't know, Half-Life was the first game that Valve has ever released. The game started the success of Valve that resulted in many game classics and Steam (on which you are now reading this review).
Half-Life itself is a first person shooter. The big difference between Half-Life and other first person shooters is that instead of just shooting, it also has exploration parts through puzzles and platforming. What I really liked is that nothing in the game takes the control away from the player. You go through the entire game and choose what to do by yourself at any given moment. The game doesn't have cutscenes and the story is experienced through gameplay and dialogue. But you can also just walk past all the characters in the story and just continue. I really appreciated this, because if you die you don't have to listen to what you already know. That makes following the story optional, even though there is only a little bit of story given which is basically just: You work at a research lab and everything went wrong. Try to escape. Many parts of the story are mysteries  you just have to figure out by yourself throughout the game. I only got annoyed once due to a scientist explaining what was already shown to me through gameplay.
The first experience of playing Half-Life felt a little bit boring. The loading for areas was really annoying, and I thought the game didn't look all that well. After a while though I got into it, and I didn't stop. Thanks to this game, I have a new insane record of non-stop playing without leaving my chair for 13.2 hours, until I completed the game. I guess that also has to do with the fact that it was my first day of my vacation, and hadn't played a game for a long while.
What makes the game so much fun is that you feel so free because nothing is told and you have to figure everything out by yourself through gameplay, which is really satisfying. I never really got stuck for a long while, because everything you find in a room has a reason to be there.
The shooting is also fun and gets even more fun over time. The only problem I had, which might just be a personal issue, is that I think the weapons were not very well balanced. For instance, I wish the shotgun did more damage to make it an instant-kill up close. What I also liked is that in the game there are enough exploration parts and different roads to take, which resulted in me knowing  I haven't seen everything yet.
After I finished Half-Life I found out that Valve has updated this original version of Half-Life with better textures, sound and other stuff so that explains why it is easier to look at the old things after a while and be amazed by what Half-Life really is.
In conclusion, I can say that I still recommend playing this updated version of the original Half-Life. What makes Half-Life special is the variety of shooting, puzzle solving and platforming and the lack of hand holding throughout the story and the entire game itself. Playing through Half-Life can make you think about whether we took more steps backwards than forwards with the games nowadays.
P.S.

Add another game to the list of titles that absolutely destroy Thief in defining the stealth genre. Shadwen is an excellent stealth-gaming experience (Have we not all been waiting for another actually decent gme within this genre?) that gets nearly everything right, while still being creatively and mechanically unique and interesting.
Firstly, before a stealth-action game, this game revolves around a giant escort mission. Our assassinating protagonist, Shadwen, is accompanied by a young girl, Lily as she attempts to carry out her contract against the king. Your actions, namely killing or distracting guards will have an effect on your companion if she sees you exacting your sick fantasies on the plentiful peons populating the map. Your relationship to Lily is also tied to specific achievements depending on the conditions of the end of your playthrough.
Speaking of achievements, in truly typical fashion, the achievements indicate 2 or 3 playthroughs necessary to collect em' all. The achievements correspond to a genocide and pacifist playthrough, and finally a group of achievements dependent on the protagonists' relationship.
Mechanically, the game is quite interesting, revolving around this massive escort mission, but also incorporating a time-control mechanic whereby your game-over states are reverted by rewinding time and this can also be used to correct mistakes (think Prince of Persia). Furthermore, the physics engine is quite fun to play with, distracting guards with the tug of your hook on a box, dangling/swinging from a platform to dropping a barrel on poor Leeroy's skull.
Shadwen is not without its detractors though. I found every level melded together terribly, and felt exactly the same. The escort mechanics are excellently implemented however, I did still have difficulty averting Lily's eyes to my massacre on my violent playthrough. This got to the point where I would work the levels backwards, killing the guards at the end - beginning to give me time to hide bodies and such.
The story is nothing to glare at, in fact, stare away, or jam some music during the "cutscenes" and loading screens, actually, just play some music the whole way through. The dialogue, and cutscenes are dry, and boring. The only redeeming factor from all of this is the artwork shoddily slideshowed throughout, which, awesomely enough can be enjoyed with your music.

While I enjoyed the previous pirate games, I'm glad they pulled it back to it's roots of running around a large detailed city with a bunch of fun stuff to do.  I'm really happy all the hunting, sailing, finding a million dumb collectables is gone!
The only thing they stripped out too much and was missing to me was the modern day stuff.  They stripped it all out and I do miss that part - maybe not how it was handled in the pirate games but how the modern day stuff was in the original couple games.  I did like the crazy Lucy story.
The DLC was also a nice diversion once the main story was over - finding a piece of Eden really took me back to the original games.
In Summary: Highly recommended

It's been a nightmare.  I gave it a shot despite the many bugs.  Uplay wouldn't let me launch the game unless the game was installed on the same drive as Uplay. So, I had to use 45 GB of SSD space to play this game which was annoying because this is the only game that does this. I verified the files, redownloaded onto other drives, etc...but the only solution was the SSD. Strike 1.
After that I gave the game a start.  Frame rates weren't bad, but not great. 980 ti and 6700k at 1440p and i was getting in the 60s, but there were noticeable drops.  There were also numerous bugs in the game that were so annoying that I contemplated uninstalling the game.  People would randomly pop-in all of the time, they would walk through walls and tables, some would pop in with different outfits after a few seconds.  Arno would grab invisible ledges.  The edges of some people during cut scenes were straight out of the early 2000s.  No joke, one person's face had three jagged lines as his outline. Then the running was so buggy.  i would constanty run through people, but get stuck running in groups of people.  Strike 2.
Since I installed the game on my SSD I deleted the extra DLC the game came with to save about 4 GB (the kings one).  Yay.  Well, not yet.  After deleting the DLC, I went to continue my game but the game wouldn't let me continue unless I downloaded the DLC again.  If I continued with the game it would erase my saves.  So I downloaded the DLC again and the same notice came up that my saved game would be erased unless I downloaded the DLC. So I deleted some extra content the main game didn't need and it wouldn't let me continue unless I downloaded it (which I did), but the game still wouldn't let me continue unless it erased my saved game. Strike 3. Uninstalled.
I gave it a shot, but there were too many issues. What I did play was fine.  The world looked pretty, but the issues I faced were too much. I got the game while on sale and I wouldn't even recommend buying it unless it's $5.
Edit: So I pushed through all of the errors and bugs in the game so I could finish it. I mean, I spent money on it so I should. Around sequence 9 things got rough. The assassination missions got significantly more difficult and what do you know...there's no checkpoint system at all.  The game says it's saving after some scenes, but whenever I died it would take me back to the beginning of the memory.  Until sequence 9 I guess I ddin't notice there were no checkpoints because I did the missions pretty easily. I never rage quit and I rage quitted so hard during those last missions. A mix of the enemies being OP and spotting me too quickly and combat being so wonky made it really frustrating.  If the game's controls and stealth were more accurate it wouldn't have been that bad. It wasn't even that it was hard, it was just a grind to redo 20 minutes of work multiple times because I couldn't parry quick enough (which isn't accurate) and die.

Stardew Valley is a very Harvest Moon-esque farming game with a couple unique aspects to it such as mining and fishing. You get the choice of where you want to focus, although there is one option that is
more profitable than the rest. You can spend your days farming crops for money, mining for resources, or fishing
The game also features all sorts of villagers to bond with and even marry if you want to take things that far, from a shy bookworm to an unstoppable monster made of beer and everything in between, including multiple wizards!
+PROS+
+NPCs each have their own lore and unique personality.
+Diversity of gameplay elements, although farming is a far better use of your time than anything else if you want money
+One of the best soundtracks I've listened to, if not the best
+Good graphics for being pixelated
+Diversity of areas, from your farm to a beach to a witch's haunted swamp to multiple mineshafts each with different decoration depending on how far down you go
+Great destresser/pastime
+Runs fairly well with little lag and very few bugs/exploits
-CONS-
-Not much replayability. You'll have done pretty much everything there is to do by ~250 hrs, and that's being generous.
-Different 'farm' types are each geared towards a different skill, but once you play each of them, you will see that the default is by far the best. You'll want to stay with one character on the default farm to do the most.
-Different gameplay options are present but not balanced well. Growing and selling the right crops for a season will earn you hundreds to thousands more coins than all of the other four major activites combined will earn you throughout an entire year. Most early-game decisions have a good choice and a bad choice rather than two choices that will benefit certain playstyles should you choose to take them. The only exception to this is deciding whether you want to complete the Community Center bundles or join Joja and pay them money to do what the
at the Community Center would take items from various activites to do for you - either is viable seeing as you have one season where you can't farm to do some fishing, mining, etc.

This game is a fantastic descent into madness.  That madness can consume you if you’re not careful.
Those with compulsive tendency may want to avoid this game all together.  I don’t have 150 hours over about a month because I made great decisions.
Once you’re hooked on the basic gameplay, you may spend hours theory crafting different party combinations in your own head as you gradually become obsessed with completing the long and arduous task that is this game.
There’s elements of the game that are so severe I will not play it further.  At 150 hours, I can play through any of the high end dungeons now because I understand the damages and hero abilities.  It took me about 100 hours just to get a good grasp over party combinations.  You cannot test party combinations except for in a dungeon however. This means every dungeon has a good chance of death.
At the end of the game, you cannot test party combinations except for in a champion level dungeon.  That removes a very enjoyable part of the game.  Great combinations are key for completing this game and your left with a real time commitment if you lose a key member of your roster trying to test out a new party combination.
In my case, on the second to last mission in the game, I lost a party member early.  This lead to me losing my tank.  I had one in reserve that was killed in a subsequent mission because I was facing a boss I had never seen before.
Bad luck can mean many additional hours of grinding.  It takes about 5 hours of constant play through to level up a new party.  That means any losses at your top tier mean real hours of play through to get back to where you were to even attempt the dungeon.  Even the best prepare party, if you make a single mistake you can lose a very valuable member of your team.
I recommend the game because of the art style, challenge and mid game.  I didn’t enjoy beating it at the end.  It felt more like a job than a game.  I became attached to my little people and I kicked trash can s when they died.  This is because I spent 20 hours just making them perfect to either lose their mind mid dungeon or die horribly to some random event.
Play responsibly.

Originally I wrote a fairly negative review since I was rather angry with some of the issues that burden this game. I retracted the review since I decided to run a good bit of Long War 2 before I made my decisions. While this review is going to adress vanilla game my decisions are strongly influenced by the mod community and in particular Long War 2. Without that I probably wouldn't play this game ever again.
This is a sequel to XCOM: Enemy Unknown, where you lost the fight, and now you fight from a conquered society as rebels. The situation might change but the gameplay overview is still the same. You manage resources, you make research decisions, you manage other 'countries' (havens), build your base, level your troops and so forth. There are various changes and improvements over the previous game. I'm gonna go over those first.
One is that most missions you start concealed. This lets you sneak around and perform an ambush on a patrolling enemy squad. This significantly changed the overwatch camping inching from the previous game. You can gather information easier and therefore have more control on when and how you activate a pod. Even if a mission doesn't start you concealed you can bring a soldier that has 'phantom' ability and starts out so nevertheless. Next is Overwatch is FAR better. No more of your entire team shooting at a dead corpse. If one unit kills a target, others won't waste their overwatch shot on it. I can't express how good this change is. Classes in vanilla are similar to those from EU. Perhaps slight tweaks (like support class become a more remote hacker/medic type class), but more or less the same. Psi trooper gets their own specific class, and in vanilla they are probably overpowered once fully online. Long War 2 goes way beyond everything in vanilla, just like in LW1 in comparison.
Most aliens make return, but some perhaps with slight changes. Sectoids, Mutons, Berserkers, Sectopods etc. While humanoid ADVENT join and make a bulk of their forces this time around. It will make the engagements different (especially in LW2), when you have humanoids running around with rocket launchers, grenade launchers and have very specific and deadly OW capabilities. Overall tactical flavor in this game is definately not lacking.
So what went wrong? The technical portion of the game is a mess. Line of sight bugs are NUMEROUS, and at times can make your mission go down the toilet. Your unit has los on a unit in cover. You destroy that cover, now your unit somehow magically doesn't see the exposed/flanked unit. Or You get cover just 'wearing off'. All of a sudden your unit in full cover stops registering that it is in cover and counts as exposed. There are MANY of dumb instances where game doesn't behave as it is supposed to, clearly buggy behavior. It can ruin missions. If you are playing this game (and LW2) I suggest that you don't run Ironman. I personally am fine with losing troops, I'm fine with making a mistake and activating poorly, but I'm not ok when I lose a mission to a bug.
Then there is optimization. Hoo boy is this bad. I have a 1080, i7 7700 and I will get lag spikes in some activations, animations or when particle effects are numerous. Sure it is a turn based game (and Long War 2 has a LOT more♥♥♥♥♥♥than vanilla game), and yeah the game looks pretty good, but not THAT good that it should tax the hardware so much. Honestly unless you crank down every setting and resolution you will probably suffer performance issues with machines that aren't up to snuff.
The biggest saving grace for this game is the modding support. There are absurd amount of mods. From amazing quality of life mods (gotcha again), to cosmetic mods, to outstanding UI mods, to complete overhauls like Long War 2 (which i honest consider the base game at this point, since I'm never playing vanilla again). You can also go into the files and tweak setting to how you see fit. Overall this lets you expand and cater the game to how you would like it more to be. More complex, or less. Harder or easier, it is all in your hands.
So my overall judgement is if you plan on playing this for vanilla I can't endorse it.  The game doesn't offer enough options and gameplay when faced with such technical issues, but if you want to mod it (doesn't have to be Long War 2), I would then say go for it and you will probably find something you can spend hundreds of hours on.

Another suberp XCCOm title - after running through Enemy Within again, I grabbed this on sale and what immediately hit me was the difficulty levels.   Essentially it's like they took the difficulty levels from XCOM and moved them all up two levels.  I played through it on Easy and started on Normal and it was kicking my♥♥♥♥♥(though I'm certainly no strategic mastermind).  And then there's Long War 2..  it's probably the gaming version of flaggelation.    Certainly up there if you want a challenge on top of a challenge.
That aside, XCOM 2 takes all the good points from XCOM:EW and spins it around, adds some additional elements and shines it up with a bit of spit & polish.  It's kinda interesting how some of the strategic elements change now that you're the one conducting invasions/attacks as opposed to the defender.     I also like the dynamically generated mission playfields which makes every mission unique.  No matter which difficulty level you play it on, the main storyline seems a little short, but you can delay this a bit by flying around the planet and ignoring some of the main storyline missions until you are happy with your level of equipment/research.  The final mission is fairly long relative to the other missions, and can be fairly tough, particularly if you are using Ironman mode.  I also added all the DLC and that also adds to the difficulty when enabled - particularly the "bosses" who can pop up at the worst of moments, but once downed, can result in some nice gear additions.
It's easy to lose hours of a day on this game, with that familiar "just one more mission" pull that many will be familiar with from the first game (or the 16-bit originals) and while I've still not managed to get off to a good start in Long War 2, I'll definitely be back to try again.

This game has left me in awe, as it is the most underrated game I have played. I honestly had anticipated refunding it, because i could not imagine a game being decent with such a low metascore. I cannot speak to how Shadwen was at release, but now in 2017 it is a solid stealth game. Shadwen should be described as a physics based stealth game in which you are the master of time. If you desire to play a stealth game where you keep restarting the entire level so you can achieve some score which arbritrarily values your abilities, then this game is not for you. It should be understood that the reason you have this wonderful time ability is because Shadwen has a challenging mechanical complexity that would not be achievable without it. (with any input devices that exist today in 2017)
Those of you worried that this is "AN ESCORT MISSION", I promise IT IS NOT. I hate escort missions in games as well. In Shadwen you arent protecting anybody other than yourself, you just have what I see as the ghost of your innocence following you in the distance. (the ghost girl cannot be caught or cause you to fail in any way) However if you play as a pacifist it is about navigating the ghost between npcs,  requiring extreme patience. (even playing as a pacifist doesn't exactly feel like an escort mission.)
Shadwen is easily worth twice its current sale price of less than 5$. It might actually be my favorite stealth game, even though I am a fan of the Hitman series and many others. The physics interactions create a range of scenarios that are challenging, but also very dynamic in how they can be approached.
My biggest complaint is the graphics,  I expected the lighting to be much better as the Trine series have fantastic graphics. (TO THE DEVELOPERS:>>WHY IS THERE A DUMB CIRCLE SHADOW WHEN YOU ALREADY HAVE SHADOWS BASED ON THE LIGHTING? WHO DOES THAT?)
Overall I love the game and recommend it to anyone who has enjoyed a stealth game in their life.

This is up there in my Top 3 Best Mods of all time. Easily.
The changes made to the base game aren't earth-shattering, and upon close inspection of how those changes are implemented, it quickly becomes appearent how simple and rudimentary thier construction is in most cases. The changes are basically achieved with what amounts to a digital "spiral notebook and some still photographs of new textures". But with those simple tools, the cats behind DayZ:Mod have really sunk thier teeth in and hit the zombie survival nail on the head.
This isn't your "L4D: KILL IT ALL! KILL IT ALL WITH FIRE!" button masher. With DayZ being built ontop of what can be classified as no less than a tried and true "Military Personell Simulator" (without even a fraction of the paper work and ten times the unaccounted-for munitions.)
When I played EVE Online, I figured it would be many years before I saw a game even pretend to compare to the treachery it inspires in its player-base. But DayZ may have perhaps surpassed the deceit of EVE. Not in scale (the scale of player-betrayal in EVE is second to none) but in how immediate, and visceral it is force-fed to new players. And its a self-sustaining beast, since players who were initiated so cruely, tend to turn around and laugh harder and be more cruel to the next guys. And this can really ruin games like this, and can instantly rob people of thier entire evening of what they thought would be enjoyable play time to test out some of the mechanics, and replace that with having to wade through the mud and the rain for five miles back to thier corpse. After having been mercilessly made fun of as if we were born yesterday for not knowing an entire wiki cover-to-cover on our first day, and simply wanting to talk, make new friends, and leave some of the game to be discovered naturally through first hand experience. I'm often made fun of for my stand-point here, and ridiculed with "Aww, poor baby doesn't like dying."
I genuinely don't mind dying. In fact it can spawn some really fun and exciting nemesis situations between rivaling players. But a line has to be drawn, players should be given a chance to get thier feet wet, grasp the mechanics, or survive long enough to see thier buddy(s) log in to play together. Don't feed the beast guys...work together...even if you aren't on the same team. Theres no reason to be inconsiderate or rude. If you don't understand this concept and it seems contradictory to  you, give it a couple years, wait till puberty ends. You'll get it.
In the mean time, if you can recruit a friend, or manage to make a new one (in all honesty) there are some incredibly enjoyable mechanics in DayZ, with the backdrop of an often gorgeous and engrossing environment that I often find myself just kick my characters legs out on the side of a hill and watching the rainstorm. Very few games have been good-looking enough to make me wanna do that, but Arma2:OA is definitely one of them, as well as DayZ.
If anyone has trouble surviving the plethora of errors and installation pitfalls, I'm usually willing to offer any help I can. And if you're interested in joining a group / server with me, I'm always on the look out for mature, calm players that enjoy the cooperative prospects of online games like this. Even the most knowledgeable and technically savvy players will require quite a bit of help in grasping / manipulating one of the most UN-intuitive interfaces I've ever seen, again easily comparable to the GrandCanyon'esque "learning curve". And even if you've been warned of everything that can and will go wrong, things will still stop you in your tracks and have you scratching your head. Many of the in-game menus are a bit convoluted, much of the environment is in Russion, and many things often have an almost "unfinished" feel to them. But that being said, I can admiringly say that the good certainly out-weighs the bad in my book. Just don't come alone ;) Bring a friend. Buy an extra copy or two. And work through it together. It's definitely not a 12 year olds CoD weekend-warrior FPS game.
This is a cruel, harsh, unforgiving, cursed mod for an already teeth-grindingly difficult simulator of sorts. But with a little luck, and a helping hand (trust NO ONE for your first entire week, no matter what) maybe you'll uncovered the addictive, immersive, awesome-fest of DayZ

Wowza. Half Life, woah. Well, back in the day, Half Life was the start of something new in FPS's. What that is, exactly, cannot be put into a simple sentence, it's even difficult desribing it in a whole review!
Some of the features you get with Half Life: Fluent controls with fun action and much more.
The story of Half Life is very interesting. You see, you are a scientist that works for Black Mesa (a scientific research lab for a bunch of cool stuff), during a certain test with a portal thing, all Hell breaks loose. There are aliens EVERYWHERE, scientists and security guards are dying, and, to make matters worse, some marines that are coming to """save""" you come down to the labs. I mean, all of this stuff is going on, and you just want to leave. Gordon Freeman (the player) doesn't speak, nobody knows why, but he doesn't.
The gameplay in Half Life is extremely fun and action packed; even by today's standards. I'd say it's better than some of our FPS games today! You can pick up health and charge up your HEV suit, a suit designed for specific tests that go on in Black Mesa. A fully charged suit can make you survive a LOT longer then with just health, as health easily drains without suit power.
You have a very wide selection of weapons in Half Life; from a crowbar to experimental energy weapons. Each weapon has their own unique use. For example: The crowbar is useful for killing weak enemies such as headcrabs and wounded enemies, it can also be used to easily open crates. Some weapons are better for close range (shotgun, assault rifle?, and crowbar), and some for far range (revolver, that one energy rifle thing, crossbow, Ghostbuster gun).
The enemies in Half Life are actually pretty challenging to fight, the marines specializing in ranged combat and explosives and the aliens with melee and more energy attacks. Some enemies, such as the headcrab, are very easy to kill, but are found in larger numbers.
Music the music in Half Life is pretty good, but there is no constant music, which is pretty nice.
Online multiplayer, yeah, that's right, online multiplayer. Well, asside from the troubles of finding a server, the multiplayer is pretty fun and I actually kind of love it. So fun. But the only problem is that barely anyone plays on Half Life servers, they're playing their newly-fangled TF2 and CS:GO, whatever those are. If you get the Ghostbuster gun, then you are the best player.
Overall: 10/10. Iz rely gud

Shadwen is a stealth game where you escort a little girl (Lily) through guard-filled levels, whilst on the way to assassinate your target.
This is a giant escort mission done right: Lily never ruins the game for you, the game is entirely designed to be an escort mission, your actions influence how Lily sees you and you can order Lily to move somewhere.
The game is highly replayable, because it fully supports a pacifist playthrough and an all-kills playthrough. I've done both and am happy to say that the game works equally well in both styles.
There is a rewind time mechanic, which encourages trying different options. I'm always tempted to try something ridiculous, because if it goes wrong I can simply return to a few moments ago.
There are some minor problems:
1. The levels don't feel particularly different and you'll end up doing very similar actions to proceed through areas. However, the game is reasonably short (approx 6 hours) so this isn't too much of a problem. It would have been nice if they'd included  a level that entirely took place on rooftops or underground or a prison, etc.
2. It's not altogether clear why Shadwen would compromise her mission to guide Lily around.
3. The guards completely ignore Lily, so why does she need escorting around? I'm glad the guards ignore her, but from a design perspective it doesn't quite make sense.
These are small things and they don't stop me from recommending this game.

enjoy this chicken stir fry recpie
- Serves 4
- 10 mins to prepare and 10 mins to cook
- 325 calories / serving
- Healthy
INGREDIENTS:
- 1 orange, zested and juiced
- 2tbsp soy sauce
- 2tbsp sesame oil
- 250g (8oz) tender stem broccoli
- 5cm (2in) piece root ginger
- 1tbsp sunflower oil
- 1 garlic clove, finely sliced
- 1 red pepper, deseeded and thinly sliced
- 150g Straight To Wok Noodles
- 400g (13oz) chicken fillet, cut into thin slices
METHOD
Step 1 - Mix together the orange zest and juice, soy sauce and sesame oil and set aside.
Step 2 - Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain well and set aside.
Step 3 - Finely shred the ginger. Then heat a large frying pan or wok, add the sunflower oil, heat it until sizzling, and fry the ginger till it's crisp.
Step 4 - When it's done, remove with a slotted spoon. Add the chicken and garlic, and stir-fry until just browned. Remove the meat using a slotted spoon and set aside.
Step 5 - Add the red pepper and broccoli and stir-fry for around 2-3 minutes until it's just tender. Add the soy sauce mixture, bring it to the boil then return the chicken to the pan

Before you buy this game you need to realise that this is not a full HD remake of Colin Mcrae Rally 2.0 but a port of the mobile phone version, which contains far less content. 3 different rally zones, Australia, Greece and Corsica. It also only has 4 drivable cars, the Ford Focus, Subaru Impreza, Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution and the Lanica Stratos. Whether more tracks and cars will become available later down the line, I don’t know.
The menu design is rather clunky and is clearly designed for a touch screen device and there is no tuning section for your car and no replays after each race. There is however a section for repairing your car after 2 rally stages although as far as I can see the damage on your car does little to how you perform during a race.
As for the racing the controls are okay, the graphics are also okay however some of the textures such as the walls can look very ugly, alot of the sprites also look fairly blend eg. Crowd members and trees. To get round this there is quite a bit of motion blur which does make the game look smoother at times.
The pyhsics of the game are also okay but not great. There is some visual damage to your car when you hit objects, but this could be improved massively. There are also inconsistences in the track I found myself getting caught on flat bits of land and getting flung up into the air with no real reason.
Finally the speed, when I first started the game I thought I hadn't set my car up correct because it seemed so slow. In many rally cars you find yourself in constant battle to keep the car under control, however here you can hold down the gas/acceleration button for the majority of the time without having many issues.
So my thoughts this game is okay at best, but it could of been more, should of been more. It should have brought back the old school Colin Mcrae Rally 2.0 memories. But this game simply doesn't live up to that title and that’s a shame.

PROS:
-The AI accumulation system which makes enemies behave differently as the value goes up.  The bigger enemies are a very real threat.
-Tight controls and game mechanics.  Jumping, dashing, shooting, punching; everything's responsive and quick to pick up and they're all used to their fullest throughout the game.
-Having a game entirely about robots and mechanical stuff which not only avoids overdosing on the color grey, but has a decent amount of color to mix up the visuals, namely with the title character.
-The sabotage system allowing parts of the ship to go down at once or later, which makes certain platforming sections or corridors easier by disabling certain things.
CONS:
-This is pretty clearly designed with a controler in mind.  Using a keyboard took lots of trial and error shifting the keys around to find something sort of comfortable.
-It can be a bit frustrating to get through most of a room, die, then get sent back to the entrance and have to do it all over again.  I wouldn't change it, it's just frustrating is all.
-Final sequence is a bit meh.
Overall I do like this game and am currently going through new game plus mode.  And a tip for anyone speedrunning this: If you're on a conveyor belt and look up so the belt is offscreen, it behaves like a regular platform.

I received this game for free from Free Games. It is a comedy action RPG featuring an archer Alesha, a staff fighter Dobrynya and a sword and shield fighter Ilya who decided to band up together to help the nearby farmers and villagers with wild animal and bandit problems.
This game is easy to finish, with an estimated playtime of 10 hours provided skillpoints are not used until a game save is made and the save is used to obtain all the 3-star achievements for each character's skill. Combat is simple and easy for most of the game where each character's normal attack is enough to defeat most enemies. Some of the fights get a bit more difficult where Dobrynya is at an obvious disadvantage against archers and sword and shield enemies who can strike very fast and slow him down. Most of the skills in all 3 characters are also not very useful, with only a few skills that are really needed to raise to 3 stars to win certain types and groups of enemies. Furthermore, when the other 2 heroes are following the controlled character, their AI could be better in helping to defend the player from enemies attacking them from behind. Quests have sufficient variety and humour. Although all quests have objective markers shown clearly on the game map, some quests become impossible to progress and complete due to faulty NPC AI pathfinding.

Graphics and soundtracks are decent. Recommended when at discount or bundle offer as the game has a few bugs that might be annoying.

Shadwen is your character set out to kill the king with the company of a little girl named Lily. I love the feel of this game. I love the ambience and the night time theme of it. I have to say at this point, if you are looking for a high action, hi paced game, this is not it. This is a stealth game. So if you are looking for something sort of laid back, then this is a good one to have. The music as well is pretty good, it really makes you feel the game more.
So we have a cool feature where you can TOGGLE stop/start time. It's default on stop, which means time only moves when you move. This is great because not only is this a stealth game, you have to stragetize your way through it. You cannot simply just run through it and thats that. If you get caught, you can REWIND your play to any point, all the way to the beginning of the stage if you want. There are two ways to play it. Get through the game without killing any guards which is what I did first and is pretty challenging, and then get through the game killing all the guards which for the first 7 maps, is pretty easy, but starts to become challenging when you have to think of your next move and how to follow up for the next one.
You are also guided and have to guide at times, Lily, a small child you rescue in the beginning. As you clear the way for her, she will run from one hiding spot to the next. She does this automaticaly so sometimes if you are not sure where there is one, just distract the soldiers and watch where she goes. Luckily the game doesn't end if Lily gets spotted, otherwise this would really be frustrating. There is an option where you can select the field vision of the soldiers and it looks like the light of the second coming of Christ, coming out of their eyes. Really a huge benefit, but even more challenging for those who disble them.
There are times that you have to guide lily, because she runs back to her previouse hiding spot if she gets spotted, you can call her back when the soldier had changed direction or somethinig, but you have to piont to where you want her to go.
All in all, a good game for the Winter Sale 2016. Excellent graphics, great music, and a fun game play
I can say this, it does become a bit redundant, but the game has only 15 levels. So it's not a long game.
It does have a lot of potential, I'd certainly be curiouse if there was to be a Shadwen 2...
***** Bonus Escape the Castle is the whole game done backwards. No achievement on this, so you can play how you like, kill all, sneak all, or combo of both. It doesn't matter.
But I can say, it is more of a challenge. There are more roof top opportunities and you really have to strategize how you are going to get through and pass. Do you kill or distract? For me, distracting worked better than killing, and vice versa.
So an interesting gameplay for sure.

There are a couple of issues I had with the game (more info below), however with the amount of time I've spent on this game, overall it's worth it. Ill say I recommend this game, but only at a sale price (I purchased this for $4.24 in the humble store). Now, the review.
Shadwen is a stealth game. You play Shadwen, an assassin who’s goal is to kill the king (for reasons not entirely explained). You bump into a little girl named Lily who wishes to tag along with you, which turns this game into a long escort mission through the castle’s grounds. The most notable mechanic is that you can rewind time (much like Braid). You have to use this when you die, or mess up at any point in a level or want to try something different. This is especially good for those who aren’t that good at stealth games. The game’s events does have some flexibility.
This game is advertised with the inclusion of a level editor and workshop support, which is awesome, and some of the player made levels look really interesting. However, not only is the level editor only for the windows version (only on Steam, as a review on the GOG page pointed out, and for reasons I completely understand), the
,
If that’s the case, why doesn’t the store page reflect on this? I really appreciate and thank Frozenbyte for bringing this and the Trine series to Linux, but at least disclose the limitations the Mac and Linux versions have.
With all that being said, for the price I paid, I would still recommend Shadwen.

My Tower Unite Review:
If you didn't know, this game is the sucessor to GMod Tower, which was one of the biggest mods for Gmod.
Tower Unite has definatly improved since its release date. I love this game so much, it is one of my most favourite games. I'm now going to show you all the stuff you can do in Tower.
Gameworlds: The Gameworlds are amazing. I'll show you all the gameworlds now.
Minigolf: Kind of like Golf with Your Friends, but with hat customization.
Ball Race: If you have played Super Monkey Ball, you should know this gamemode. If you havent, heres a short explanation. You're in a ball and you're trying to get first place and collect as many melons as possible.
Virus: Like Call of Duty Zombies, but scarier. Short explanation: You're with your friends, but one of you're friends got infected. Try to stay away from the infected and live as long as possible.
Ok, thats it for the gameworlds. Now onto the Lobby.
Lobby: The lobby is the main meeting place in Tower Unite. You can meet up with you're friends and meet new friends. Lets list some of the stuff. WARNING! The Lobby is not done yet. So if you see anything with a COMING SOON sign, Just remember that this game is in Early Access.
Ok, ok. Enough about the warning, lets look at the stuff you can do in the lobby.
Trivia: The Trivia is a gamemode (not a gameworld) where you have to answer some questions and you get Units for it.
Casino: You should know what a casino is. Lets not talk about it.
Theatre: Now when you think of this, you think of going in there to watch movies. But you are wrong. You can watch videos in the theatre. (via, YouTube).
Ok, Last but not least, You're Condo!
Condo: Your condo is you're own personal space that you can customize with stuff you bought from the lobby. There's not much to do in the condo, so here's one thing you can do.
PARTY!: Invite you're friends, get together and PARTY AWAY!!
Ok, thats all you can do in Tower Unite.

Darkest dungeon, a story of love and hate.
What may attract you at first is the pretty artstyle, and the dynamic turn based combat, added with that epic narrator voice.
Beyond the look, you will find enjoyment in facing difficulty,  learning how to overcome it and the tension rising each turn.
But after every mistakes you will be testing your resolve and your will to play this game again, because it means another characters that you spent time on did just vanished, back to dust. Which comes to the main problem of Darkest Dungeon which is the lack of control on the game. In a few seconds everything can happen if you don't play carefully.
Many people believe this game is way too rng based,which is true, but you got total knowledge of every probability, you know the numbers and you can increase them, giving you keys to progress. But sometimes, even unexpected can happen. You may feel the game is not balanced and not fair due to pure bad luck
This problem matters more towards the endgame, there is a huge and sudden spike of difficulty and bad odds that breaks completely the will to play and finish the game.
You can go beyond that, and discover the wonderful world of masochism and madness, or stop playing, feeling bad because going so far into the game and loving it, and yet you won't go further.
I would like to note that there is a cool modding community that adds a lot of content, new classes, mechanics (even some that makes the game easier! you coward), dungeon. And that's free.

This game was sitting on my wishlist for quite a time and, to be honest, I wasn't that much interested in it. Chantelise and Recettear, both also Carpe Fulgur's titles, seemed way more appealing to me than Fortune Summoners at the moment. But since I have a soft spot for pixel art games, I finally decided to give it a go and bought it along with the other two. If I were to judge only by the screenshots, FS seemed like a cute platformer with a few RPG elements. And it kinda is exactly that, but the RPG elements are way more predominant than I thought. Sana and eventually Stella, Arche's companions in all of her crazy adventures, are pretty much essential since, in the early parts of the game, Arche's attacks don't always flow well and it's very easy to get knocked down by strong enemies. But once you get the hang of the combat and some new abilities, things get much, much better. There are some puzzles in the dungeons, and most of them require that you switch forth between the girls, each having an unique ability necessary to deal with the situation at hand. Arche is the easiest one to control in combat, tho. The story is as simple as its characters, but FS delivers it in such a charming way, with a pacing that feels sorta like a slice-of-life anime, that you find yourself truly enjoying it despite all the cliches. Overall it's a solid game if not an unpolished little gem.

Don't mind what people say about this being an RNG-fest. Okay, it kind of is at times, but if your strategies or plans mostly rely on one or more dicerolls they were bound to fail anyway. If you don't have contingency plans for when things go south, it's kind of your own fault if you have your party wiped out.
Just think ahead. Think of the possibilities. Think about action and consequence. What is safer? Having your healer heal one of your heroes before that last enemy can kill them off, or trying to let your healer kill said enemy before it can get another hit in? Would potential stress be worth the potential HP healing if you let one weak enemy alive at the end of a battle? What are the chances of an enemy getting blighted vs an enemy getting stunned?
Pick your expedition carefully, and your parties even more so. Failure will be inevitable, but luckily you'll always get more chances. Still, don't be afraid to cut your losses and run if necessary. Like the narrator says: "The sin is not in being outmatched, but in failing to recognize it."
It's a hard game, but also very rewarding. Pounding hearts as you try to kill a boss with your last standing hero, realizing and learning from mistakes and triumphing over enemies that once kicked your♥♥♥♥♥are all parts of the game. Victory is worth it.

It's kind of a shame to me that this game is notorious for its difficulty when there are plenty of popular side-scrolling hack n' slash RPGs that are FAR more challenging, with very good reviews, like Dead Cells, for example. I assume the misconception is based around the idea that you should charge in at every monster you see. Patience is definitely an important part of the adventure and often times you should make sure you're fighting monsters 1x1 rather than trying to take on several at once.
The controls can feel clunky at first, but once you get used to them you will find that they are very smooth and precise. I think the trouble that people have with it is that there is slight buffering so that if your character is performing an attack and you enter more commands, she will perform the next command once she's done with the current one, rather than ignoring it, as some other games might do.
With all of that said, this game is everything that I love in an action-adventure JPRG: The story is quaint, the characters are likable, the music is charming. The scale of the story isn't "gotta save the world", and instead is localized to a couple of towns (kind of like the Ys series). The adventures that the characters go on feel almost nostalgiac -- it's not unlike kids in real life who might go explore some woods or a creek, but then make sure to come back home in time for bed (because they can't exactly stay at an inn). It's cozy, in a way (difficulty aside).
Anyway I don't think anyone should let the difficulty of the game keep them from playing it. You can't rush through all of it, that's for sure, but it's not like you can't grind if you absolutely need to.

Stardew Valley at it's core is a simulation game in the same vein as games like Harvest Moon.  You run a farm, you look to make profits, you interact with the town.  Stardew Valley offers the player tremendous depth and variation in how they want to play the game.  You can farm, you can forage, you can fish, you can dive the mines and kill the monsters with in it.  An experience system allows for perks at certain levels to give even greater variation in how you want to play the game.
There is a lot offered by the game and it ultimately is up to the player how much they want to explore and take in.  At a surface level it is simply a farming game, but like all great games, it becomes hard to put down due to its depth and charm.

The story is a pretty generic "young children help a lot of people by collecting magic things" plot.  The graphics are fairly nice, in my opinion.  There are some light puzzles and platforming, but it's mostly about the combat.
And oh boy, it's the combat that shines.  Even battles with run-of-the-mill slimes are interesting.  They can and will predict you.  Fortunately, you are given a lot of moves, from stabs to flying kicks.  It feels rewarding to defeat monsters, even if you don't get much stuff from it.  Some enemies may be tougher than intended (see: flying enemies), however.  Even so, this is some of the best combat I've played in any game.

Huh, I realized I never did a review for the first time I played this. Well since I just recently replayed it, I can give a fresh review of it now. To put it bluntly, this is a fairly good game, but you really have to dedicate time to playing it.
Both playthroughs I've done with this game on Normal with auto-block on (back in 2013) and Hard with auto-block off took me around 20 hours to complete. This game is a pretty big grind just to even progress through the game, but just normally exploring dungeons to the fullest should net you enough experience beat the game.
Now to talk about the most important aspect of the game, the combat. This game, while being an action/RPG, actually has elements of a fighting game sprinkled in. You got guarding and dodging, you got fast and slow attacks, you got combos, and you got enemy AI that actually reacts to your inputs. It's all there! You can choose between being the main character who uses a sword, a fire mage, and a water cleric, so there's vareity available to you if swordplay isn't your forte.
But is the combat good? Eh...kinda? I mean I like where they're going with genre mixing, but my biggest gripe which unfortunately dampens the entire experience is the controls. There are many times when I input moves that just for some reason don't happen or are apparently overwritten due to frame animations from the previous attack. It also doesn't help that dodging is fairly unrealiable and you're better off blocking until you can counter. It's a mixed bag, but overall, I had fun.
And the last thing I want to talk about is the story with no spoilers. All I can say is that they build up the world by spewing out exposition on different locations and fresh potential adventures...only to have the game end aburptly. To me, this is the biggest disappointment of the game. Near the end of the story, it sounded like your adventure only just begun, but nope, the game just ends. With no sequel or additional content so far over 5 years since the game released (in the English version), it hoenstly made me feel like all the grinding and effort I put into the game was for nothing. And that's definitely a bad thing.
However despite these flaws, I can barely reccommend this game for the gameplay alone. It's definitely fun to play around with, but just don't get your hopes up for a satisfying resolution at the end. Get it on sale.

This program is extremely versatile. It has a very slight learning curve because of how very indepth and flexible its features and options are, but it is truly a necessity if you have two or more monitors, and need to use them in different ways!
For me, I use it with my old Wacom Cintiq 12wx (a drawing tablet with a monitor) as an illustrator/artist, which has a lower screen resolution than my main monitor - but the main monitor sometimes has to become a "slave" to the Cintiq (and thus, its screen resolution) when cloned. This program lets me switch to have different resolutions quickly (when split), change which is the master/slave, etc - not to mention what program/apps go to which monitor by default, etc.  All at the click of a button!
I'll likely be adding another monitor soon for my hobbyist music recording as well (y'know, when you got your tracks on one side, and your mixer on another), which is gonna require a whole different monitor profile setup. =)
Multiple monitors can really help the workflow for about any gig or hobby, I think, and this program will really make your life that much easier. If you're looking for a challenging platformer with fast paced action and robot combat, you've come to the right place!
The Zarnoks are destroying several planets in the galaxy, and when their target become Saphirium, your job as The Guardian is to protect it from complete annhilation!
In fact you'll have to rush through the spaceship-fortress in order to sabotage critical areas and be able access the core and stop the invasion, and you'll be fighting against the clock. Depending on the difficulty, you'll have different amount of hours and sabotage areas (on normal it's about 7 hours, you got time!), this makes you feel right into the action, as you slowly watch the fortress approaching the planet and killing the inhabitants, it's a touch of "realism", a real invasion must be stopped as soon as possible, to save as many people as possible.
The best part of the game is the platforming and robot fights, you'll need every bit of skill to rush in every section of the fortress while dealing with the robo guards. You can take a stealth approach, or just charge the enemies and give 'em a good ol' uppercut in the robochin :D
The map is huge and interconnected, it does the job well to recreate a spaceship and the feeling that is a whole "world", which is cool, although sometimes, and that's the only problem I had, it feels a bit confusing at first, there are many directions you can take and it'll require some time to understand properly the structure of the spaceship.
There are also hacking sections, which is the second kind of gameplay you'll face, that is navigating the fortress' net, unlocking doors and collecting data, that will weaken the enemies' AI for easier fights! (I like this feature, very meta!)
Overall, if you like platform games with a touch of metroidvania, I highly recommend you this game. It's fun, runs fast and furious on the platforming and combat, and it is challenging nonetheless, it'll test your ability as a true savior of the galaxy!

Brigador is super fun game where you pilot a mech/tank/hovertank/vehicle–with-mounted-weapons and take on a missions with fully destructible environment in an isometric perspective. There is a lot of lore to read (it's well written and interesting) and a lot of gameplay modifiers (a lot of vehicles, with different weapon loadouts, and various pilots) to unlock and use. The game offers a sense of progression as you unlock stuff. There's a campaign mode with a tutorial and some missions with set parameters. There is also a freelance mode, which is more like a sandbox which can last a number of maps depending on how you set your run.
The vehicle types feel different and control differently (the game is based on tank controls) but there are a lot of control options to tweak them to your liking. I play with a controller, and I do just fine. The vehicles themselves offer a lot of variety, have cool visual designs, and awesome lore associated with them.
The artwork for this game is amazing; I've never enjoyed looking at portraits so much. The UI is also quite pleasing. The music is also amazing (awesome John Carpenter-style 80s synth), so the soundtrack DLC is super worth it.
The devs are also very friendly and approachable. They still support this game, and have had two free content updates so far. I can't believe I didn't know about this game when it first came out. It's shocking how it went unnoticed.
Wholeheartedly recommend.

I was really interested in this game because I really enjoy stealth games and the whole point of this game is to not be seen. Like, so much that as soon as a guard spots you, you're dead.
I thought that seemed interesting enough and bought the game a while ago. Keep in mind, I haven't even played for an hour and I'm sure when I get "used" to it, this might be an okay game. But still, I have already come to the conclusion that I will not be recommending this game. Even if it's only two things that bother me.
Let me just start with the positive: it's a pretty game. You get to play both characters (Shadwen and ... I think the little girl's name is Lily?). I haven't gotten to a part with them together yet, but I know it happens later on so that's great. Uhhhhh. Yeah. No glitches, no lagging. I don't know, that's about it.
Then there's the negative: you can rewind time, and freeze it. This makes a stealth game stupidly easy. It doesn't challenge you, really. Sure, maybe you gotta try out something a few times to get the timing just right, but when you realize you're about to get spotted, you rewind time (with seemingly no limit as to how far you can rewind), and you're safe. And even if you die, you just rewind. It doesn't throw you back to the last checkpoint (which MIGHT be a good thing if you die a really annoying way and it's far from the checkpoint - we've all been there). But it gets a bit annoying most of the time.
The freeze thing. It's not that you click something and freeze time, no. It's when you stop moving. And this is fine in the first part of the game, when you're learning (even though, even then, it gets old pretty quickly). But this seems to be a part of the game that will stick with you throughout the whole game. I tried to go into the settings to turn it off, and I might've missed it, but it seems like it's not possible to turn it off. And I like to get into the game when I play it, y'know? Like, it's like you go into this fantasy world. It doesn't feel like that when the game screen goes half-grey and blurry every SINGLE. TIME. YOU. STOP. MOVING. I loved Altaïr and the first AC when it came out and I loved Ezio even more. Assassin's Creed seemed to be the franchise, that was built for me. Then came revelations and I was disappointed to the level of not even considering to buy Brotherhood. I scorned all the sequels and went back once I had read about Black Flag, which pulled me back into AC's glorious days. What I had learned was to carefully research reviews and opinions prior to an impulse buy, which costs you being part of it from the beginning and not being able to argue when friends and buddies all talk about it. AC Unity got plenty of bashing through reviews and first buyers alike, though it kept fascinating me just through the still pictures I saw online. I waited until it was bugfixed and patched and I didn't regret having added it to my collection.
True, there are some minor glitches still and it is also true, every 3h of gameplay Arno won't exactly do what you where aiming to when pushing the controls (sidenote, I am a mouse / keyb gamer). Sometimes NPCs pop out of nowhere, but the whole experience is so immersive that it all won't matter. Hiding and planning your next move, analyzing patrol movements, carefully trying to achieve all challenges from the mission objectives and levelling up to get better gear, skills and outfit made me long for the next treasure and the next chest. The world of AC Unity is utterly overwhelming at the beginning where never ending missions, secrets and the like fill your map. It is most disorienting and luckily I am not a completionist. The story is compelling enough to keep you going and the fights are a tough nut to crack (why that's probably my first AC where I really specialized on stealth). The game is incredibly rewarding if a mission goes well and no alarm was triggered. It provides a sense of plain satisfaction. The French Revolution as a setting is breathtaking by just walking through the streets and wondering about it's marvellous architecture. Though I cannot claim its historic accuracy, the mix of it with some hollywoodish intermezzo just makes the trick.
The game will keep you busy with plenty of extras outside of the main story, where you're requested to complete rifts, which is some kind of data collection parcours, investigation quests where clues will lead you to accuse one of many suspects and the solving of puzzles to gain access to special armour, or you can plan a heist in a well protected villa to gain more loot than by just roaming the streets. They're all optional but seemed more than a filler to me and are truly engaging if you're committed to let it sink in. I would buy the game again just to walk through French Revolution Paris once more and would make it mandatory to have the city and it's crowd being visitable via VR to every history class professor. I didn't do any of the multiplayer part since nobody ever seemed to play either at my level or was trying an online game while I was.
What I especially liked
+ fights are very hard, but smooth and nice to look at
+ special skills like transforming yourself into a target
+ the utter beauty and vivacity of the environments
+ the tons of options to configure my own Arno to my playstyle
+ sidequests like the Paris stories
What I didn't like much
- I felt like I missed a lot by not chasing every potential map entry, but I got tired at some point
- That's personal flavour, but I missed the real world Abstergo parts Desmond Miles got me used to
- Another personal flavour, the tombs and treasure hunts felt always like an arcadish challenge and I missed them
- The story builds up nicely, but ends a bit abruptly and feels flat (and I didn't understand it to be honest...)
Other than that, I would recommend the game anytime.
Cheers, adre

I picked up the game while it was on sale. It took me roughly 13 hours to beat it and get all the achievements.
The game consists of a few fun mechanics:
1. Time moves only when you move. This reminds me a lot of Superhot, and it makes planning your next move much easier.
2. You can rewind time as you wish. This extremely feels like the Prince of Persia Sands of Time series, but you can rewind infinitely, so getting stuck in a unsolvable situation that you dragged yourself into is impossible.
3. Guards can see and hear you, and will walk around when alerted.
4. You can use the environment to alert guards by attaching the rope to things and moving them.
Sadly, there are some flaws that might ruin the fun for you:
1. Checkpoints only work at the end of the level. When you continue your last save game, you will ALWAYS start at the beginning of the level, no matter what savepoint you previously passed. It literally says "Saving" and when you exit the game, it claims the last save was "0 minutes ago" but still, it will reset you to the beginning of the level. This is a minor nuisance, but still leads to playing the same parts over and over again.
2. Gameplay-wise, there is NO variation at all. The game is one giant escort mission. The level design is quite alright, but playing roughly 8 hours of escorting will wear you out.
3. As usual, the escort AI is stupid and will often not do what you want it to do. Also, the AI sometimes knows in advance when a guard will turn around and start running uncontrollably in some direction. Fortunately, the AI cannot cause you to be discovered - the girl can LITERALLY stand IN FRONT of a guard in DIRECT VIEW and nothing will happen (apart from the girl turining around and going back).
Another redeeming point is that rewinding, sound discovery and stealth in general works really well - you cannot get into unsolvable situations and guards will not have a lingering memory of what happened a few seconds before (many games suffer from this problem). Also, lethality will correctly work with rewinding - except one weird glitch, enemys never died without me deliberately killing them.
The voice acting is great (both guards and the main cast) and the sound design is okay as well. The game has a great setting and a lovely story, but there is really not much story in it, which is a pity!
With a recent update, they added a reverse chapter, where you break out of the castle. I haven't tried that yet, since I just finished the achievement hunt.
All in all, I recommend this if you
- like stealth games
- have a high frustration tolerance
- don't get bored easily
- can grab it for less than 5€
