TLDR: half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥cash-in with no redeeming qualities, 1/10, do not buy, Codemasters should be ashamed.
I really don't understand how Codemasters managed to screw this one up.
Sure, they definitely indulge in milking old franchises (Worms, anyone?), but this game claims to be "based" on Colin McRae Rally 2.0. CMR 2 was/is an AMAZING game, a benchmark for rally games at its time that has aged exceptionally well. How hard could it possibly be? Take that game, port it to a modern engine, maybe nix a car or two and replace decals if you can't get hold of the same licensing deals, and you've got a great game, done!
But no...
This game manages to be so basic, so stripped down, that it barely even qualifies as a racing game, let alone something that should be mentioned in the same breath as CMR 2.
Cars: CMR 2 had over 20 different cars. This game has 4. Yes, four.
Courses: CMR 2 had 8 countries/courses. This game has 3. Yes, three... To make things worse, the Australia and Greece courses are basically the same gravel track. The Corsica Course is 100% tarmac. That's it. All races are in daylight, no rain. Compare that to CMR 2, where you had rain stages, night stages, snow courses, mud courses, hardpack and loose gravel courses, etc...
Controls/physics: Pretty much any jump will send you into a barrel roll. There's a glitch that appears pretty often where while climbing, the car will suddenly "snag" onto the track like it's a piece of fabric, and lose all momentum. Wonder how many hours has been put into playtesting...
More problems:
- The cockpit view. MY GOD. You'll have to see this one for yourself... I'm dead serious, the Sega Daytona USA arcade machines had more detailed cockpit graphics! CMR 2 for PC came out in 2000 and it had a fully detailed cockpit for each car, what the hell happened here?
- If you look at actual PC (not console) screenshots of CMR 2, this game does not look better in any regard, it actually looks worse... much worse. Much worse than a game from 2000...
- Absolutely no pre-race tuning, which was a major part of CMR 2 and was pretty much obligatory to get good times at courses. But I guess it wouldn't be neccessary in a game like this anyway, where the courses are as varied as peas in a can.
- At this point mentioning the lack of replays, additional game modes etc is pointless. This game would still be a steaming turd, with or without more content.
Multiplayer: nope.
Controller support: if you have anything more exotic than a 360 pad, you're out of luck as there are no remapping options.
Please, DON'T repeat my mistake and buy this.

Short version: A fun, enjoyable side-scrolling 2D action game with some RPG elements and puzzles, only held back by the occasionally confusing combat from being truly great.
Long version: There's a lot to like about Fortune Summoners. The sprite art is just lovely, you can see a lot of love went into the graphics. Even the main characters' idle animations perfectly reflect their personalities. The characters themselves are, well, little girls who go on adventures through caves and dungeons. The story, told mostly through dialogue boxes, is fairly simple and straightforward, but charming in its own way. Talking to NPCs is mostly optional, but it reveals more about the characters and the world they live in. They even have to ask their parents for permission to go out adventuring!
The gameplay consists of controlling the party of one-to-three characters. The players controls only one character at the time, the AI controls the others, and it's possible to change the controllable character with the press of a button, even in the heat of battle. Technically this means it's possible to attack the enemy with the melee character, switch to the fire-throwing mage and burn them until they're dead, and finally switch to the healer and bring everyone's HP back up.
In practice, it's more likely that the player sticks to the melee character (the main character of the story) and just lets the AI handle the others. The AI does a good job and doesn't require handholding, and it's even possible to tweak the AI settings per character.
As the story progresses, the party visits several towns to heal up, stock up on items and purchase new equipment, while also exploring dungeons searching for whatever they need to find there, as mandated by the narrative. Naturally, there's enemies abound, which leads to the game's most problematic part: the combat.
At first the combat feels great. As the sword-wielding main character, the player has several different attacks at their disposal: Down + Attack for a quick forward thrust, Up + Attack for an upreaching swipe with which to hit flying enemies, and so on. More sword techniques are learned as the character levels up, requiring slightly more complex button combinations. At this point the combat feels nice and methodical: block the enemy's attack, thrust, slash, block again, roll behind him, slash some more, and so on. It's fun.
Unfortunately, at some point the enemies become numerous (though never more than 5-6 at a time) and the combat often becomes a confusing mess. Colorful spells fly, enemies swoop and jump around, the AI party members do their own thing, and the player is left wondering just what is going on. This isn't helped by the fact that some enemies can trap the player into a loop: they pick the character up, toss them down, then come back for another go or three before the character can even get up. The enemies can also dodge attacks proficiently, and it feels if the player and an enemy attack each other at the same time, the enemy's attack always has priority. This can be quite frustrating.
The game's dungeons can be large, and there are no maps of any kinds available, so a good sense of direction (or making your own maps) is recommended. Some dungeons also have puzzles that need to be solved, mostly of the block-pushing variety. But they're never terribly hard, so they don't kill the flow of the game.
With a run through the game lasting about 25 hours it certainly has a nice length to it, but in the end I was personally getting weary of the combat. I'd still recommend the game, though.

Bugs, dodgy UI decisions, and some supposedly core mechanics that defy the games core philosophy.
That philosophy is a good one, reward the players ability to assess and manage risk on multiple levels, with many hidden/not obvious variables at work that are there to significantly reward you for doing something "right", and more lightly punish the "wrongs", missions are risky stuff, but if you open your eyes, ears & mind a little, are always within your control more so than ADVENTs.
Hacking & Stealth mechanics were not given this treatment for whatever reason, their success or failure is largely out of the players hands unless they plan to alt-f4 or reload a save.  Which will get boring real quick and put you off these mechanics, because those load screens are looooooong.  Hacking especially is far more advantageous to the enemy AI than it is to the player, especially if you attempt the t2 hacks, the enemies rewards for your failure massively outscale your own rewards for success, and it costs the player a valuable specialists action points for the turn too.  Xcom would not actively train specialists other than for combat roles if they were being practical under these conditions.  They might turn that GREMLIN budget over towards teaching their veteran soldiers how to just check their damn corners & ledges for once in their short lives.
Gripes aside, Chess 2 is a great successor to Chess 1 and I would pick it up the moment it next goes on sale.  The problems i mentioned can be fixed (other than the terminal case of loading-screen) with some ini edits and/or community mods very easily, and should be.  Grab yourself a copy of notepad++ while you wait for the download, you'll want it for later.  Personally recommended only because tweaks are easy, fix the balance issues that I percieve, and allow a really impressive degree of customisation.
tl;dr good game but don't bother hacking something unless its close to 100% chance or has no failure penalty and stick to the center of the roads for stealth because reasons.

Buggy, rambling and dull.
I can understand some of the appeal of the game - it's a simple task-based format, focuses on a small area, and allows the character a lot of autonomy in what they do. The map is useful, and in many ways it is fun to whack trees and rocks, plant stuff, 'talk' to the other characters and generally explore.
However, I also found it incredibly frustrating.
- There is very little help available in-game; once you're told how to do something once, that's it, nothing else. I even needed to look up the controls to understand how to interact, as it's not particularly intuitive.
- I found various bugs impeded me: for example, I could not get fishing to work, and very often found I was unable to interact with items unless my character was in exactly the right place.
- While there are quest lines available, there is very little direction and once you are given these quests then that's it - the information on them is limited and if you forget (or, as gamers do, exit the game and return) you then have to return to various places to get information again - if you can even remember who gave you the quest!
- I also found the day-cycle incredibly frustrating - it apparently takes half a day to have a conversation, and it meant that my ability to explore felt artifically limited.
I'm sure that if you can get this to work, and get deep enough into the game, then it's great. But for me, even four hours of playing was too much frustration over any enjoyment I got. Not worth it.

This is what you get when you mix Thief, Super Hot, and PoP Sands of Time... It's Thief with the mechanics of things only move when you move, but also with the ability to rewind time if you screw up.
It's not the greatest execution of any of the mechanics, it does them all ok at best, but everything working together makes it an enjoyable stealth puzzle game where the stealth is more of a "how do you do it" puzzle and not as much of a "I know how to do it, its just executing it that is harder" since things only move when you do its not about perfect timing like games like Theif, Hitman, and Deus Ex would require. Yes you do sometimes have to fastforward or rewind time to get the gaurds into the perfect spot to distract one without getting them all, but its not like say Hitman where you have to wait 3:27-3:31 to do something or you miss your oppertunity.
All in all nothing about this game is great, but everything about it is atleast good to fair and all the peices work well together even if it could have been better, there are definitly a lot worse games you could spend $17 on, this game is not a must buy, but you won't be disapointed with a purchase either.

I dual screen with my TV, on Win10, and this app is great for it.
A good trick to keep mind is:  if you turn off multi-monitor taskbar, and leave the taskbar on your left monitor, the icons will stay.  Sometimes when one monitor shuts off they all go over to one side or the other (stupid windows).  But, when it does that, if you unlock your taskbar, and drag it back tot he other monitor, your icons go back.   Or, you can use the built in icon location save/restore feature in this app.  Probably easier just drag your taskbar back the one in the blue moon this happens, as your dekstop icons change over time.
If you set your right monitor as your "primary" display and move taskbar and everything else to your left, your fullscreen games will awlays start on the right monitor.  right/left/center, it's all the same, you get the idea.  This lets me keep a "desktop monitor" on my regular screen and a "game/netflix" monitor on my TV.
That's not to say that this app isn't useful.  It's actually all kinds of useful, with a lot of neat features.  I think my fav feature so far is that it works with Win 10, and lets you set diff backgrounds for each monitor.  You can even set folders for it to randomly cycle through.  How cool is that?
Another cool trick is, if you don't use your desktop icons all the time, just right click your desktop, click view, and uncheck "show desktop icons".  When you want your icons back, just check the box again to show them ^.^  I mainly use my taskbar for things, but I do use my desktop now and then.  And thank god that uuuuuugly fullscreen start menu is dead in desktop mode in 10.
Win10 is still new, but works pretty well from what I've seen in being backward compatible, This great app fills in a lot of missing features in backround/desktop management.  My thanks to the developers for keeping it up to date and compatible.

Shadwen is a stealth game in which you sneak past or stealth-kill guards while on an assassination mission, all while escorting a little girl with you for really no good reason. She's all "Ima follow you, gurl! You can't stop me!" and my assassin chick is all "Okaaay, but do what I say," when she
have simply replied "Um yeah, I have a grappling hook that'll let me cross town in seconds while you have stubby little girl legs and can get your butt kicked by the city watch. You do what you want, but you'll never see me again. Now eat these friggin' apples and go away."
+ Time freezes when you don't press a button, so grapple-swinging from thingy to thingy is pretty fantastic and even managable for players lacking actual skill (i.e. makes it more of a mental practice for the player than a physical one).
+ You can use the environment such as rolling big, wooden barrels or breaking wooden crates to distract guards.
+ You can hold R to rewind time if you die or get spotted or whatever! It's great and far more time-saving than checkpoints and loading.
+ Graphics, music and sound are decent enough.
- The whole game is an escort mission. Almost everyone on the planet dislikes those. They're like water levels and sewer levels; generally unenjoyable.
- You are warned that the story is impacted if you kill with the little girl around...and she's always around. So I'm playing as an assassin and can't kill anyone in the game if I want the rainbow happy fun times ending. We all know the ending where you do the mean thing is almost always crap compared to the kindness ending.
- You can't even do non-lethal takedowns! I'm stuck doing distractions and putting myself at far more risk than knocking guards out and hiding their unconscious bodies. It works in Deus Ex, so it should work here. I should be able to club guys over the head.
- Waiting on the little girl's derpy AI to catch up can get you killed. There are doors you have to stand beside and pull a switch with Lily simultaneously. If a guard is patrolling or returning from looking into a distraction and Lily is caught on the game's environment/geometry, then she won't pull the lever and you get caught, and it's not even your fault.
- Uninteresting World-Building/Historical Setting. If this is in our world, the game doesn't make the history interesting or meaningful. If it's in a fantasy or similar world, it doesn't do anything to make that world intriguing from what I witnessed. Although I didn't play very long, the game needs to hook players in and make them want to see more of its world in this sort of game. Deus Ex, Dishonored, Thief (the old ones)...all of these series make cool places you want to explore and learn more about. I didn't care about this game's world because it didn't try to make me care.

Half-Life is one of the most important games in video game history.  It basically gave a name to "Doom Clones" and sticks with alot of gamers over the years.  Why?  Well, theres alot of reasons.  Half-Life's emphasis on strong gameplay and unique storytelling is great.  Your no longer a badass soldier murdering demons on mars or some hero without a name or background, your Gordon Freeman, a scientist at Black Mesa.  Basically, the right man in the wrong place, ;).
It teaches you the mechanics without needing a tutorial, I mean, there is one, but you don't have to do it, lol.  It slowly introduces you to weapons at a good pace and gives you a chapter to play around with them.  Before the last few chapters where they dump alien weapons on you at every second expecting you to know how to use them, XD.  The level design is awesome and allows for multiple choices when in combat.  The story isn't anything new and is actually really bland by today's standards.  You can choose to take part in the story or not, because it's told by the other scientists.  You don't even have to talk to them, which is nice for speedrunning and replaying the game.  But Half-Life isn't about the story, it's about immersing a player into a creepy and unkown setting, putting them on the edge of their "gaming chairs" as they shoot tanks, aliens and helicopters.  It's a very atmospheric experience that I highly recommend and is one of my favourite FPS games of all time.

Where to start.
Brigador is an isometric vehicle action game in which you are a pilot from one of three factions given a unique opportunity to make a large sum of money.
Solo Nobre is a city on the colony world of Solo Novo. Years ago, control of it was seized from the sponsoring corporations that founded it in a militant uprising led by a man known only as Great Leader. Great Leader ensured his control over the city by erecting a series of orbital cannons meant to ward off any invasion from above while his armies secured Solo Nobre through military force and the division of the city into walled districts. All contact with the outside world and the galaxy at large was cut off, with Great Leader's watchful cannons ensuring the security of Solo Nobre.
This seizure of power was not without opposition. At the end of the Nobrean Civil War, a surviving band of revolutionaries, the Corvids, began to slowly rebuild and make plans of a new revolt, for they believe that the only way for Solo Nobre to prosper is under a free and democratic government. This goal, to them, must be reached no matter the cost.
The Solo Nobre Concern, a shadowy organization created by the founding interests of Novo Solo, wish to retake their rightful property. That's where you come in.
Tonight, Great Leader has died. The Loyalist Military under his command is in disarray, and the Corvids have taken this opportunity to launch their own uprising and have already seized several districts. In addition to this, the Spacers, a transhuman mercenary element from Deep Space have arrived upon Novo Solo in search of profit and glory. You are a Brigador- a paid mercenary hired by the Solo Nobre Concern to carry out certain military objectives within the confines of Solo Nobre, with the end goal of liberating the city in one night and allowing it to shelter once more under the umbrella of economic prosperity provided by the SNC.
Whether you're a defecting Loyalist in search of passage offworld, an opportunistic Corvid looking for personal gain, or a ravenous Spacer thirsting for glory and wealth, only one thing matters tonight.
Great Leader is dead.
Solo Nobre must fall.
Here is your Contract.
Do you accept?
=================================================================
The game itself is fantastic. Smooth controls (they may take some getting used to, but alternate control schemes are available in options), beautiful visuals that look like a proper evolution from a 90's action game (unlike so many "retro" games these days, who simply awkwardly pantomime the style), and a fantastic soundtrack (by Makeup and Vanity Set) that immerses you starting from the main menu.
You have a vast selection of vehicles, weapons, and special abilities that will aid you in your mission to bring destruction to Solo Nobre, and the three factions each have their own selection of platforms across three types (Mechs, Tanks, and Antigravity Vehicles). Each faction also has a wide selection of pilots who serve as difficulity and income multipliers, as well as revealing intimate background information about themselves and the factions they serve.
The writing is superb, with the background slowly coming into full view as you unlock equipment, pilots, intelligence entries on enemy vehicles, and a good spread of dediated lore entries as well that elaborate upon the world of Novo Solo and the galaxy at large. If you enjoy the sort of storytelling where everything isn't immediately apparent and you must work to unlock the world's secrets, then Brigador will satisfy you.
One final thing that I personally appreciate is that the Devs are very active in the game's discussion forums, and won't hesitate at all to listen to your comments, or answer any and all questions about anything related to the game and its development.
On top of being a fantastic game, it's going to be growing even further. The Devs have announced that on June 2nd they'll be rolling out a re-release that adds more vehicles, pilots, and a redone tutorial campaign as well as an entirely new campaign. Whether anything else will be hiding among these goodies, I can't say, but I know that I'm looking forward to June 2nd. It will also be going on sale then, which will no doubt encourage many more to try it.
If you like gritty science fiction, kick♥♥♥♥♥action, amazing electronic soundtracks, and fantastic writing, give Brigador a chance. I doubt you'll be disappointed.

How to drown a good game into disgrace.
Having the original Colin McRae Rally 2.0 since it came out, all I expected was to be able to play it fully in my actual machine without learning rocket science. Well, I have to recognize that has been achieved. You can play it... at least the parts you can...
Megabazillion tracks... errr nope: The original game brings us 9 countries, (Kenia, Finland, UK, Sweden, Australia, Japan, Corsica, Greece and Italy) each with twelve stages. This rip only brings Australia, Corsica and Italy. By now, The game duration's been cut to a third.
Megabazillion rally cars... errr neither: The original game places us behind the wheel of 24 rally cars, counting WRC, B group and various paint schemes. Here there are ONLY FOUR STINKY CARS. Content reduced to a fifth.
Then, the controls. I'll agree Colin McRae wasn't the most realistic rally game in history (we have RBR for that), but at least you can figure out what is driving a WRC. Here, the controls are almost random. The car cuts gas in the middle of a straight without any reason at all, and the turns are divided into two: you did it or you didn't (There's no way to negotiate a drift)... Basically, I found out that I can't drive the car as I want (as in the original), but instead I have to learn how the game wants me to drive it.
And then, the graphics... well, even worse than the original (the internal view is worth a shot, don't miss it), plus the scenary has been cut to a size that looks more like you're playing Gran Turismo 1.
In a nutshell, don't set your hopes any high: It's an awful port, ripped everywhere, and almost unplayable.

Como desgraciar un buen juego:
Teniendo el Colin McRae Rally 2.0 original de la época, lo que esperaba era poder jugarlo completo en el PC que tengo ahora sin tener que andar haciendo experimentos. Bueno, hay que reconocer que eso si se ha logrado, Jugarse, se puede jugar. Lo que se puede jugar...
Pistas a go-go... pues nó: El juego original nos permitía correr por Kenia, Finlandia, UK, Suecia, Australia, Japón, Corcega, Grecia e italia. Este rip no trae mas que Australia, Corcega y Grecia. De momento, la duración del juego se ha reducido una tercera parte.
Coches de rally a go-go... pues tampoco: El juego original nos pone a los mandos de 24 coches, entre WRC, Grupo B y esquemas de pintura variados. Aquí no hay mas que CUATRO APESTOSOS COCHES. El contenido se reduce a una quinta parte.
Luego ya está la cosa de los controles. De acuerdo que Colin McRae no era el juego de rallies mas realista de la historia (para eso está el RBR), pero por lo menos te podías hacer una idea. Aquí los controles son prácticamente aleatorios. El coche deja de acelerar de forma incomprensible en medio de una recta, los giros son una de dos: o entras o no entras (no hay posibilidad de negociar un derrape)... En resumen: me he encontrado con que, en lugar de conducir como yo quiero, tengo que aprender a conducir como el juego quiere.
Y los gráficos... pues muy justitos. Comparados con el original son incluso peores (la vista interna del coche es digna de ver), y encima han restado profundidad al escenario de una manera que parece que estés jugando en gran turismo 1.
En resumidas cuentas, no te hagas ilusiones: Es un port horroroso, recortado por todas partes, y prácticamente injugable.

Okay. So i played the crap out of this game. As you can see at my play hours.
I understood and learned a bunch of things about it, so let's get started:
The game takes place 20 years after the Defeat of XCOM in the original game, going from a timeline where they lost their base at the hands on the alien Invasion. From there, they now work at a salvaged Alien Ship, from the looks of it seems to be one of the Heavy class ship of old. Earth is now subjugated and you are the leader of the resistance forces who fight against their rule. You, the Commander, must fight back against a new and sinister enemy know as ADVENT, an governemnt organization created by the Coalition between humans and the Alien Elders, while trying to stop a secret project that could be the end of mankind.
GAMEPLAY ASPECTS and thoughts on it:
> The RNG and POSITIONING
-Tactical based gameplay similar to the original game, but improved. More organized than the previous titles.
It requires not only strategic thinking to turn odds to your favor, but also a little bit of luck in a RNG dice roll. That said, the RNG is heavily influenced by how you are positioned and protected.
You will not hit every shot, and the aliens can hit you with some lucky shots, however both of you are governed by the same rules, with the veteran difficulty balancing the tip towards your favor with "Miss Streaks" and "Aim Assists" for your soldiers. At higher difficulties, those differences cease, you and the aliens obey the same odds.
A bad positioning effectively means your defeat, and a strong positioning can lead you to victory. Keep that in mind while playing and you will find yourself depending less on luck and more in how you place your troops. (It may happen the hilarious 95% chance miss, it's not frequent and quite rare, unless the game really decided to hate you all of a sudden).
> SKILLS and ABILITIES
-Abilities are important, as they can bless you with guaranteed hits you will definetly need in some situations. It can turn the tide of battles very quickly to your favor. That said, the enemy can do the very same things with their abilities should the circunstances present themselves. Two units close to each may result in a grenade flying towards you. Or one of the powerful abilities the aliens have may be used against you.
With that in mind you will understand that some aliens must be taken out first, or that will result in one of your troopers being dragged across the map or half of your squad poisoned.
Different Aliens mean different aproach and different strategies, learn your enemy in order to defeat them.
> CLASSES and PROGRESS
- There are effectively 4 default classes for your troops with 1 special class divided in two ability trees that give them different roles in combat, the abilities can be mixed, so you are not stuck with just one role or the other, and given the proper infrastructure, you can retrain them (although you cannot change their class)
- The Aliens do have different types of enemies with different abilities, however their upgrades are based around the progression know as "force level" and "Dark Events".
-> The force level effectively defines the type of alien you will face, as well as the upgrades towards aliens you already encounter. A common trooper will become and Advanced trooper as the time moves forward, and later in the game you will be facing Elite level troopers and more powerful Aliens.
-> Dark Events are strategic elements that rule over your campaign, they can last 1 to 2 months depending on the Event, or add points to their secret project. They can range from adding poison coated ammo to your enemies, or sent a UFO to hunt your SHIP.
>RESEARCH:
The research element is straight to the point, have a material, research it. Have a corpse, autopsy it. Have a thing, do this thing. You can improve your research time with more scientists.
>ENGINEERING:
Also straight to the point. You research a thing, you acquired a blueprint on that thing, you build that thing.
With the exception on the proving grounds, where takes time to construct an armor or make said blueprint. Experimental item blueprints give you a random item that can make a hell of a difference in your performance. Or building an more advanced armor that is not the default medium choice.
-TIP-
Research and Engineering can save you if you had your star squad wiped by a couple of bad decisions, however, losing missions over and over may result in campaign victory for the aliens, and you falling behind in force level category, where there's simply no way for you to face them anymore without you effectively turning a simple encounter into an epic struggle between untrained troops and powerful alien overlords.
Which most of the time will result in Death if you are not of the most experienced XCOM player.
That said, these elements make an realistic representation in technology gap, if you don't keep up with your enemy, you will get steam rolled across the battlefield. It also means that if you manage to get the Early advantage in boosting your crew Engineers and Scientist staff, you will effectively do the same thing to them, although it all comes down in how you manage your squad into battle. Once you get the hang of it, you will rarely lose a mission, maybe a soldier or two.
>STORYLINE MISSIONS and OBJECTIVES:
- There are a couple of missions that represent the Storyline progression, which are required to complete in order to reach the end and win the game. Some have the term of "catasthropical failure", which results in instant victory for the aliens should you lose it. Missions with that term allow you to restart it and try again, or restart the game with a new campaign. One of the two.
--------- In regards to DLC -----------
Alien Hunters:
- This DLC adds four new powerful itens and three new powerful aliens for you to face along your campaign. With a story element should you decide to have the complete.
-> Having the story mode selected you will have a mission that starts the scenario, the enemies will not appear until you decide to.
-> Not having the story mode selected results in the enemies appearing normaly in the campaign and the weapons appearing in the engineering section for you to build them.
Shen's last gift:
- This DLC adds a MEC to your squad. An early game useless unit but a late game monster with the technological improvements. Like the Alien Hunters, it does have an story element that allows you to start the DLC. If not selected, you will be able to build it as soon as you get the Proving grounds.
Anarchy's Children:
- A cosmetic DLC, it adds anarchy themed cosmetics to the game for you soldiers customization. The flavour is not for everyone and honestly, you can find better mods for your cosmetics. Although it has a cool piece here and there, it doesn't justify a DLC.
Resistance warrior pack:
- Another cosmetic DLC, that in it's size, doesn't justify a DLC. And for some reason is not included in the reinforcement pack.
------- Personal suggestion for developers --------
If you are planning on making a DLC for the game, i would suggest one where we could play as the Aliens in their Storyline, it seems that it has a room for expansion and will allow for a different perspective. It would introduce an different aspect to the game since the we would be playing on the Aliens Side. and will allow for some player to have a choice to subjugate humanity, or not, depending what the aliens are really thinking.
It seems like a silly suggestion but it has room for potential if done correctly.
------- Overall ---------
It's a game that is supposed to be Brutal and unforgiving on combat side, any early mistake can lead to a defeat. It does get easier over time as you progress, but even so, it's not for casual or newbies that can't learn from their mistakes. Although Veterans can have a very casual experience.
Overall.
8 / 10 for Gameplay. 7 / 10 for Strategy. 4 / 10 for DLC. 7 / 10 for Story.

When I first bought the game I put in a good 5 hour session or so on it as I found the main gameplay very addicting and captivating.
Screenshots and gameplay videos don't do the "feel" of this game justice, the mechanic of time / enemies only patrolling as you move, and the ability to rewind to any point in the past is a very unique mechanic. Somewhat like Prince of Persia series but with no limit to the amount you rewind to. It's one of the more unique stealth games I've ever played. The one hit deaths possible from any of the enemies, as well as the ability to pull objects with your whip to distract or kill guards add to the constantly shifting strategy with which you have to approach each of the levels. Add to that the ability to craft gear including mines, sticky bombs, and arrow traps, and more, and you have a pretty fleshed out package.

Just to be clear from the start, Shadwen is not a bad game. Shadwen is a game developed and published by Frozenbyte, the same people behind the Trine series
Shadwen is an odd game, cobbled together from various other mechanics and it's good that indie developers try stuff like this. However, this time it doesn't work so well. The core game plays like early stealth games. The stealth kills are fairly bland
There's a grappling hook which gets you spotted more often than not and is best used for dragging objects to cause distractions. There's a rewind time mechanic which had no in-game explanation or any restrictions pretty much wrecks any challenge in the game. There's also the "time only flows if you move" thing, it's an okay mechanic but it doesn't bring anything to a game that has no combat... there's not one single moment where it comes in useful
The game can be played as a murder rampage or a stealthy kinda deal... that would be great except the whole thing is one giant escort mission of a girl called Lily. The guards can't actually see her but you need to provide her with cover to get from point A to point B. Sadly often her AI refuses to move even when the coast is clear so murdering people is far easier than trying to stealth it
Sadly, Lily has no personality whatsoever and will chastise you between levels for murdering people. On top of that there's very little in the way of story, no character progression, HUD, skills or loot. There's some sort of crafting system but I finished the game just fine without crafting anything. It's also game over the moment the guards see a dead body...
Ultimately, I don't dislike Shadwen. It was an okay game, but that's all it is. You may get more mileage if you really wanna go through twice for achievements' sake but the level design is linear and unimaginative and the game just doesn't live up to the potential
Yet another dissapointment from Frozenbyte...

I was on the fence about whether to rate this game positive or negative. I decided to recommend it because despite the things wrong with it it is still a great game. Heat signature is a game about doing different quests in order to work towards liberating stations. Like any good roguelike, this game has weird character names. Each character has a personal quest, and using money you earn from quests you can unlock the character's personal quest. Each quest gives a certain amount towards liberating a station, and then you can choose which station to liberate, which will give you a certain item to be unlocked in your shop. This is the main mode of progression, as these items will help greatly. You can also scrounge up great items from looting ships, so always be on the lookout. The best way so far is to have lots of friends, so they can give you gifts, although this might just be for the Christmas update. Each liberated station has its own defector mission you can try. These give no rewards but do teach you how to do good in certain situations. Overall this game is pretty fun, there is a good amount of variety and replayability, and I would recommend it. Now for the pros and cons.
PROS:
- Fun game
- Good variety of items
- Although sometimes hard to solve how to win the mission, it is always doable.
- Not hard to figure out how to play
- Replayability
- Something to work towards
- A lot of achievements
- Good music
CONS:
- If you use a character too much, they earn no progress towards liberation. I understand why this is done, but I think it is a bit unfair as you might have "unique" items on that character, becoming useless
- Sometimes in space, the screen turns bright white and you can not see anything. This has caused me to lose a few characters that I spent a long time on.
- If you hijack a ship and don't autopilot, it is slow as hell and takes ages to turn. This needs to be fixed
- Out of the 4 types of pods, the more expensive ones are less useful. (sovereign coldfire, foundry brick) Let's be honest, besides getting the achievements nobody uses those two. It would make more sense for the expensive ones to be glitchers tick and offworld angel as those ones are actually good.
- The concussion hammer can be heard from a good distance away which makes no sense, as it barely makes noise.
- Some clauses can be ruined by the idiot crewmembers accidentally killing themselves. Other ships attacking can also ruin the clauses. This should be fixed imo.
- There is nothing added to a characters legendary status except stations liberated or sometimes characters rescued. There should be a bit more to do, but I don't know what :P
- Some missions are TOO easy. I had a mission where I had to steal something, and the object to be stolen was next to the door while the whole crew was on the other side of the ship.
I would love to see a co-op mode for this game, I think that would bring in more players and be really fun. It would also be nice to get more of a reward for hijacking ships and returning them to base. It's a freaking massive ship, and I had to kill the whole crew to bring it back, but it gives little to no acid, giving no incentive to do it. You should be able to see a list of ships you brought back to your bases. Also, the stronghold liberation missions are far too easy. If you just teleport to the captain and set course for the stronghold, you win. It doesn't matter if you die, it doesn't matter if you kill anyone. You don't even have to kill the captain, just swap with him. You would think the crew would have the sense to not suicide bomb a base. These particular missions are the core objective of the game, and they are easier than a good amount of regular missions. I would definitely say this game is worth it, maybe get it on sale. Hopefully a few more things are added by full release. This game should give you at least 20 hours of fun, more if you enjoy this kind of thing.

Styx: Master of Shadow + Superhot = Shadwen
Shadwen is a mavelous game and I'm sorry that I let the complaining reviews leave me hesitant for so long. It's both beautiful to look at and fun to play. But let's be clear about where I'm coming from:
--If you are a person who loves traditional stealth, loves HIGHLY CHALLENGING traditional stealth, and have no complaints with the traditional stealth genre whatsoever... then you're probably going to find Shadwen too easy and too boring.
--If you are a person who finds traditional stealth annoying AF because it is almost always frustratingly ambiguous, so you end up replaying the same bit over and over again because you can't read the game's mind? Maybe you found Mark of the Ninja really refreshing because of how not-so-ambiguous it was for a stealth game? Well then you might enjoy Shadwen! Being able to freeze time and rewind time pretty much saves you from all the classic stealth annoyances.
Also bear in mind, this is not your usual stealth game in the sense of you merely needing to make it through a level, possibly steal something on the way, etc. This is actually an---okay, bear with me---it's an escort game. BUT THAT'S OKAY. Escort missions are only ever annoying because the people you are escorting are dumb af, die constantly, and require hand-holding, but that's not what's going on here. The girl you are escorting is basically invincible and will never actually alert guards, even if it looks like they SHOULD see her. (Some people find this dumb, but I call those people persnickety. It would be annoying as hell if the game did not make her invincible this way.) Kinda like Skyrim/Fallout rules where you can trigger alarms but your companions (usually) don't. The companion you're escorting is kinda like that.
Since your companion is basically invincible/undetectable, Shadwen's gameplay becomes sort of like one of those rolling marble mazes, where you have to tilt the maze to allow the marble to roll through. Every level is a maze with a certain path to the exit. First you need to identify a path. Then you need to eliminate guards or distract guards so that Lily (your escortee) can run past them when their attention is diverted. And of course, you need to avoid getting spotted yourself. You proceed through each level this way until both you and Lily reach the exit. You cannot complete the level unless Lily makes it to the exit with you. There are various chests you can rob along the way, snatching up materials to craft helpful gadgets (though I honestly have not found much use for them except just as some extra fun to play with).
The hookshot is a central part of the gameplay, and admittedly the hookshot controls AND physics can be.... a little bit on the janky side. Sometimes humorously/nonsensically on the janky side. This would be a huge problem if the game didn't have unlimited time rewind. Since you can just rewind if some jank manages to jankify your hookshot maneuver, it's hardly a problem. It's no more strange than Skyrim's sideways horses. (Except in this case, YOU CAN FIX IT.)
The only two complaints I can say about this game so far is that the hookshot/stoptime controls are REAAALLLY WEEEEIRD at first. I didn't really start getting the hang of them until end of level 2 / beginning of level 3.
The other complaint is that you get some serious fatigue in your right index finger holding down RB (or Q on KBM) to make time flow normally. It would have been better if they had created an option to TOGGLE time stop instead of requiring you to hold the button down, but there is no such option, and you sure are going to notice. #1 reason to stop playing Shadwen for the night is so that your time-unstopping finger can get some f****ing rest.
So in the end, Shadwen is a different kind of stealth game. It's a little bit more casual difficulty with a unique focus on creating paths for a second character. Stealth purists may be turned off, but I will gladly drink their tears, because I'm having a grand old time.

When I first started the game, it was truly intriguing. Immediately, I identified it as Superhot meets Tenchu meets PoP:SoT. I played through first as super stealth, no-kill girl and by the sixth level, it was starting to gt repetative. Start at A, ditract guards, move Lily (a permanent escort) toward B ad infinitum. I was thankful when that playthrough was finished.
As a bit of an achievement ♥♥♥♥♥, I replayed the last segment a couple of times to get the "kill some and spare" and "kill some and kill" achievements and it was a lot more fun.
The second full playthrough was "kill everything that breathes" and it was a hell of a lot more entertaining! Distract guards to leave their group, dive on them from above, hide body and slowly pick them off until the area is clear. It was in this playthrough that the gadget crafting came into its own. I was willfully strapping bombs to boxes and pushing them off of ledges in to large groups and watching the corpses go flying! One one occassion, one of the explosions caused a guard to go flying so far it hit and killed another guard. Much laughter occured.
So why Superhot and Sands of Time?
Two of the mechanics in the game that assist in the careful planning and execution of levels are the ability to rewind time if you♥♥♥♥♥♥up (the grappling hook takes some getting used to) and time only moves when you do (or hold Q to advance it). It gives you the chance for trial and error, until you find your best approach.
For any other Achievement hunters, let me say that you MUST do the stealth playthrough first as Lily remembers all kills after completing a level, even if you replay it stealthy next time.
So yeah, I recommend this game, though I'd defo wait till it's on sale.

This is going to be a controversial review.
Half-Life is a great game, historically.  But it has aged poorly.
The controls of this game leave a lot to be desired.  Movement is glitchy, over paced and at times hard to judge, especially by the standards of games today.  It is too easy to get yourself into a position that you cannot get out of, even if what is blocking your way is literally only knee height, which given the light puzzle solving continuity, is easy to get yourself into repeatedly, as you explore the world to be able to progress.  The movement is such that dying or taking damage will be more likely a split of 75-25 in favour of self-inflicted damage from falling or moving onto or into hazardous locations.
The puzzle solving and progression of the game map, as well as the layout and structure is too much like a platform game.  Having at times to jump or dodge between unrealistic, incomprehensible and illogical structures that move, shift and twist.  At times I wonder if I'm playing something like Croc or Spyro.
The FPS elements are awkward and clumsy, again by the standards of today.  The sound effects of weapons are scratchy and annoying and as it's an old game, the animations aren't the best (but we can forgive the graphics).
The story element is the best part of Half-Life, and it still stands up, (to a point).  The game is clearly a mish-mash of FPS, action, puzzle solving, platform and story, with no single element being strong enough to carry the game solely.  We get glimpses of story, mostly from the commentary of individuals found in the Black Mesa complex, be they scientist, security guard or military.
In the end, I feel that Half-Life was a great game when it was released in the late 90's, and considering the age of the game, it does well.  But there are better games today.  We view this game I feel through rose coloured glasses, especially those of us that played it when it was first released.  But like a TV show that we might have watched when we were younger, playing it again can destroy the fond memories we have of it.   As such, this game is best consigned to the archives as a great game that was, and a giant of yesterday that today's games stand on the shoulders of.

I was gifted a copy of
for review purposes by the Steam entity,
or "EQ Free Games."  It's so neat to see videogames based directly on a cultural history/mythology (Slavic).  I once took a course on Russian folklore & found some familiar elements here.  Tragically, every other aspect of the game (aside from art) is a letdown.
Before now I'd never heard of
or any game they've developed.  Probably won't go for more of their stuff until I see ample proof of their improvement with time & experience - & I'm speaking as a gamer with a wide-ranging appetite for indie creations.  On paper the concept is great: three distinct heroes, an adventure & a villain all inspired by Russian lore/history.  Unique skills & mechanics for each hero.  Something was lost in transition from concept to game.
Clearly skills & targeting don't work as well as they ought.  Auto-aim penalties & poor responsiveness in player controls render investment of points into certain skill trees a waste.  The entire experience of player movement, jumping, strafing, pathfinding, etcetera is as clumsy as the combat.  Nothing is intuitive; gameplay is at times painfully dreary.
Triggers for cutscenes & events are occasionally misplaced, leading to events being out of sequence.  It'd be hilarious if I weren't actually trying to finish the level.  A few bugs caused crashes, or led to inconveniences like a missing mouse pointer or launch failure.  This doesn't alt+tab well at all, either.
I played on Normal, given the choice of Easy, Normal or Hard.  Doesn't matter all too much since combat is wonky; hitting enemies & surviving battle depends as much on whatever's happening behind the scenes as on your input!
Localization in English is fairly poor.  Grammar errors, laughably awkward voice acting, misspelled or entirely incorrect subtitles.  It just took me out of the moment.  The art style is quite pleasant - very bright & colorful with clean lines.  The music seems fine for a low budget indie; I'd say low to middling visual/audio production quality.
And yet after all this, I still found the will to play all the way through to the end.  My first attempt wasn't great.  I came back a few days later & willed myself to finish the game in one full evening of play.  Conceptually it isn't bad at all!  The game's just rudimentary in so many ways that it is at no point a compelling experience.  The single gratifying moment for me was seeing how Hero-specific mechanics were worked into completing an objective that utilized the folklore stuff.  I won't spoil it.
I don't want to be too harsh in my review; I respect the effort that goes into creating even a small game.  With design tweaks & significant technical overhaul I'd happily play, on whichever platform.  Unfortunately I can't currently recommend
.  A shame, as I was curious at the outset to see what could be done with the folklore angle.

PEOPLE GIVING MARCAS A NEGATIVE RATING MUST BE COMPLETELY BONKERS OR COMPLETELY SIMPLE...JUST DISGUSTING TO SEE THIS FINE FREE SIM RACER GET A MIXED REVIEW!
If you are on a tight budget - there is simply no better sim racer you can find with such a complete single player championship experience, only raceroom experience comes close.
There is absolutely no reason for people who are into racing not to like what Copa Petrobras de Marcas has to offer FOR FREE. The only reason this game is free is because Brazil's largest oil company Petrobras is paying the bill. Marcas is a promotional game built on a quality sim engine, by people who know how to make this engine shine better than the original programmers.
You get a FULL TC championship, with the same great handling that comes with Reizas Game Stock Car series.
If you have a FFB steering wheel you are in for a treat, as Reiza's Stock Car series has been universally recognized as having one of the best driving models in the business. The graphics are crisp and functional, without unnessessary eye candy (check SweetFX*), so the game can be played on most mid range machines at the highest graphical settings.
I was actually happy that the Marcas content was recently added to the Stock Car Extreme game, as it is one one my favorite Reiza classes to drive - being front wheel driven they require a different style. FWD is another detail some negative reviews seem to miss when they discuss handling.
As for the comment on driving views - there are many camera views (!), in and outside the car.
Before posting negative reviews, take a little time to check the set up possibilities, controls etc, and you'll find that almost anything can be set up. Same for FFB, it can be tweaked to near perfection. At best any negatives given on these issues show a lack of looking for the proper settings - read stupidity of the reviewer.
Most of the negative comments seem to come from people who are expecting an arcade racer, with basic one size fits all ez mode, game pad support, game pad friendly handling and "eye candy" visuals.
Unfortunately by doing so they completely miss the point - as non target audience of this game - and trash the game accordingly.
Pearls before swine I'm tempted to say.....
The graphics are GOOD, nice and crisp SIM STYLE, instead of the on steroids Michael Bay kind you find in most arcade racers.
Get a good FFB wheel, take some time to set up this game - my Logitech Driving Force GT requires NEGATIVE FFB to work correctly, you have to know that and deal with it. These are really essential requirements, just like installing the SweetFX* shaders to get optimal visuals.
Learn how to drive with the free copa game and soon you'll be buying Stock Car Extreme for all its other classes and tracks. Want something really different, get Formula Truck.
I own the original non-Steam versions of Reizas games, including the older GSC2012 - still cool, still on the hdd and I still play them.
Summery
- arcade racers move on (please, and stop reviewing)
- get a good ffb wheel (essentiel with race sims)
- take some time to tweak your settings (also essentiel, no one size fits all in sims)
- install SweetFX (...some eye candy)
- have fun RACING (the whole point)
- give Marcas and Reiza some well deserved love!
*The post processing effects you see in videos and screenshots are not standard, but can be easily installed. SweetFX - takes less the a couple of minutes to set up.

UPDATE: If you liked this free game and want to take a look at the full game,
, go to the game's website
page and there you can download the entire 7.1 GB game for a free 60 minutes trial.
On the same web page is a Lite version demo, it includes the same car, but with only two tracks. The good news is that this 30 day demo, rather than sixty minutes, and it's only 2.1 GB.
This is a nice game that is essentially an in-depth demo for Stock Car Extreme, another racing game from the same publisher. It's very detailed with nice features like in-depth car set-up, in-race adjustments like brake bias and lots of other realism settings. It supports a variety of racing wheels, but I did just fine with my X360 controller. The graphics are a bit dated,  but better than GTR or Race 07, which it very much will remind you of if you have played those game. The nice thing about the less than bleeding edge graphics is that you don't need an uber-rig to run the game at a nice rock solid 60 fps. There are plenty of in-cockpit and other views, and a replay feature too.
There are six tracks included, including a nice "square" oval that is a good training ground for new drivers. There are all sorts of options when racing as well. Opponents can be set to any number up to sixteen, you can select rolling or standing starts, and you can also decide whether to include practice as well as qualifying sessions.
Races can be run against a clock or by completion of a number of laps. Tire wear and fuel use can be set to normal or can be multiplied to simulate a longer session. AI driver skill can be adjusted, as well as their aggression level.
This is a nice racing game even if you had to play a few dollars for it, but for free? It's a no-brainer, download it and give it a try.

As soon as I loaded this game up, I knew exactly what I was in for. Developed by Reiza Studios, the same folks behind the excellent Game Stock Car 2013 (Extreme now) and Formula Truck 2013 series of games, this is pretty much the same thing, but on the Brazilian stock car circuit. While not familiar with the Brazilian circuit myself, I thoroughly enjoy the aforementioned games, and anyone else that is familiar with those will feel right at home as well. This is mainly the reason that I am able to write this review with such little play time on this at the moment!
So on to the gameplay! Once you're behind the wheel of either of three different car manufacturers (for now anyway), you'll see the familiar gMotor 2 engine used with these games, from the HUD to the ever-so-lovely shift/rpm gauge. Of course, these can be turned off (thankfully), which gives you a more realistic sim experience, if that is your cup of tea. And yes, you can change the view from the default cockpit! This is found in the Options > Display menu. There are a multitude of other settings that can be changed as well, from the number of cars seen on-screen at once to graphical settings. Most gamers with mid to high range machines can naturally max out these settings, as the graphics are not quite up to the same standards as Asetto Corsa and the likes. But, to me anyway, they look pretty good right out of the box, so to speak. This can also be said for the car handling physics, which are the same as other entries from Reiza Studios. And that is to say that they are some of the best that I have experienced in any racing game to date. Again, those that have played the games I mentioned know what I am referring to.
In summary, if you've played the other games Reiza has offered, you know what you're in for, and will feel right at home once you're in the game. If you're even remotely interested in racing games that are more of a simulation, then you should definitely give this a try. And heck, even if you don't like racing games, give it a try anyway. After all, how can you go wrong with a free game, especially one of this magnitude. What are you waiting for, add it to your Steam library right now!!!

Vangers, there are a few hurdles that you'll have to cross to get into this game.
first is that the resolution is locked at 600x800, its a bit disjointing when you're used to 1920x1080.
second is that the controls were obviously mapped by a programmer with very long flexible fingers, expect to spend some time slowly remapping most of the key bindings.
third it that this version of the game is lacking is any sort of manual or tutorial. expect to have no idea what you're doing for the first part of the game. mistakes will be made.
fourth is that this is a game from 1998, the graphics look like a game from 1998. it is what it is.
still with me? ok. here is what i like about Vangers:
the worlds are complex and for the most part nice to look at, the story is deep and intriguing, the controls are responsive, combat is satisfying, early in the game combat is difficult even a daunting task, later in the game you get to become an nigh in-killable tank god wizard.  the worlds are littered with secrets some of witch require you to pay attention to your counselors most of which are not easily evident in the beginning. because the game gives you so little direction when you do finally figure something out, you feel as though you've actually accomplished something. the game has replay value, I've beaten the game once on steam and three times on the original game disk, each time I did things in a different way. you'll beat it the first time and you'll want to play it again to see what you can do now that you are skilled.
I fully recommend Vangers even if you're not in to driving games because it's not just a driving game it's also an exploration game and it's a problem solving game. you don't want to pay 6 bucks for a 20 year old game? totally understandable, put it on you list and wait until it goes on sale, I paid 2.70 for it on steam. this is also technically the third time I've paid for the full game. I HAVE NO REGRETS.

If you like RPG Dungeon Crawlers and loved how XCOM had you manage your troops and see them die then you're in the right place.
PROS:
-Dark/Lovecraftian atmosphere.
-A Variety of Heroes each with their own list of skills which make party composition and skill choices important.
-Several different Dungeons with their own individual themes, quirks and enemy types.
-Resource management as you prep what to take and what to drop as your inventory fills through dungeon crawls.
-Stress mechanics adding a second layer to combat.
-Hero management through the stress mechanic as well as ailments and positive/negative personality traits.
-You feel rewarded once you learn what party/skill combos work as well as what resources work best for which dungeon crawls.
CONS:
-Quite a few of the bosses for most of the Dungeons are just tougher versions of previous bosses.
-RNG can be discouraging for newer players. (Recommend beginners play their first runthrough on the easiet difficulty as it is more forgiving)

I just finished the game, and I have mixed impressions. It is definitely not for everyone and it's hard to say what about this outwardly bland title made it appealing for me. There are MANY annoying aspects to the game. There's no map, and many sections of the maze like dungeons you roam around in look very nearly identical to each other. Enemies spam attacks in ways that are occasionally overwhelming. Status effects...are all evil. There's the constant knockdowns and the poison that won't quit. The sleep that if you're lucky only guarantees you get hit once or twice, and can otherwise disable a character for around thirty seconds. The confusion that will cause Arche to slaughter the rest of the party mercilessly! Fortune Summoners is punishing, but it isn't so unforgiving. In the typical worst case scenario you can restart at the last room transition from the game over screen. Later in the game I would just take the death if an encounter went too sour for me. Gearing up properly and figuring out the right amount of caution to approach a situation with is very helpful, but there are going to be cheap shots constantly regardless of what you do.
Some weird issues with multi-monitor setups. The game will begin to slow down when you have any menu open, it gets slower the longer you run the game. PC Gaming Wiki has a (psuedo) fix for this, but I still started to get slowdown after about two hours in session.
Outside of the combat, the game has a fairly charming goonies/rascal theme going on about it, as you run about becoming a master social engineer, breaking everyone's luggage, stealing people's underwear, commiting genocide and eating various other humanoid creatures ('canned salmon' and 'chicken leg' indeed). Adults are about as negligent as you'd find in any children's story. There's what I'd call a fairly standard RPG level of exploration, mostly hidden nooks and crannies, like you'd find in grandia or some of the older final fantasy games. Some spotty platforming, characters have a lot of momentum in movement and it takes a bit of getting used to. Definitely recommend playing with a controller. Oh and there are a number of clever, simple puzzles, nothing really challenging, but a bit creative.
Fortune Summoners is a competent action RPG, that falls short in several ways. It will challenge, it will frustrate and annoy. Some people find that rewarding I suppose. As a final note, I don't normally like to talk price, but I'm 100% confident there are better games to pick up for $20 or less. If you're curious I suggest you try the demo and if you enjoy that, well, it's bound to go on sale eventually.

Obviously Vangers is dated and most will play it mereley for nostalgia's sake. Nevertheless, this game has interesting features that make it stand out, even to date. If you remember this game, get it for cheap and relive the memorable times. If you're just curious, hopefully my review will help in your decision to buy it or not.
Now to discuss the components individually, starting with my most valued three: gameplay, storyline and replayability.
To be honest, this is a hard one to decide on, because Vangers has strong points as well as major flaws when it comes to gameplay. If you consider this a racing game, then it falls flat out on the face. Rarely do you get the chance to actually 'race'. Got into a ditch? You're stuck. Ran into an obstacle? You're stuck. Met a pesky vanger? You're stuck. Sure you can jump and shoot yourself out of trouble, but it still takes quite some practice do use those techniques in such a way that you can keep driving.
Vangers is more than just a racing game though. If you don't like doing trading runs, you can choose to do missions (tabutasks) instead, loot hideouts, combat other vangers or hunt for cirt. All these options add diversity to the game and make you forget about fighting the controls for a moment. Ultimately, if you do get used to the controls and manage to keep on the move, you really feel like a king of the road.
In conclusion, if you can forgive the difficulty to drive around, the gameplay is decent. The various activities can be fun, although if you're looking for a fun game to play, Vangers is not something that would immediately pop into my mind.
Other than these gameplay additions, there is also the storyline included, which is the next component in the discussion.
Vangers is set somewhere in the future, where humans are merely legends of a distant past. When humans gained the ability to travel to the stars the eventually clashed with a different species, leading to the creatures that are in the universe Vangers is set in.
The story may be uninteresting and confusing at the start, especially with all the unknown terms thrown at you. However, if you like stories and have some imagination, the storyline present in Vangers is intriguing. At first it will be very confusing, but as you progress, the different NPCs in the game will tell you more and more about everything that happened.
I'll try to spoil as little as possible, but when I first finished the game, it blew me away at the end. If you are determined enough to play the game through until the end, you will be rewarded with an interesting conclusion that wraps the whole storyline up.
Other than that, each mechos (car), item, creature etc. has a backstory to it as well. If you manage to get a hold of the manual for this game, there is even a story of an aspiring vanger in there. Not only is it a nice and short story to read, it also helped me as a kind of tutorial when I first played this game.
All in all, if you like stories, Vangers definitely offers you one. And visit the Zeexen often. :)
The fact that this game is still around and revamped is a testament to its replayability.
Personally I played it at least three times: When first playing it (at a young age, mind you), I didn't understand anything and got frustrated with the controls, so I ditched it. For some reason I got back to it though. At that time I could understand the story and manage to actually drive around. Many years later my memory ached and pushed me to do a full playthrough (see below) for future reference.
So yes, Vangers definitely has replayability value. Although with Youtube around, it is to be seen whether I'd ever want to play it again. Nevertheless, Vangers is / was worth its money.
Vangers was published in 1998. What do you expect from a graphical point of view?
If you love realistic graphics, there are lots of other games out there. If you don't mind counting pixels, Vangers can offer nice explosions and the joy of kicking around debris. There are also weird creatures to look at!
Vangers was published in 1998. What audio quality do you expect?
The music is nothing interesting really. There are some tracks on certain planets that do nicely accompany the atmosphere and ease the otherwise grueling driving around.

Okay. So i played the crap out of this game. As you can see at my play hours.
I understood and learned a bunch of things about it, so let's get started:
The game takes place 20 years after the Defeat of XCOM in the original game, going from a timeline where they lost their base at the hands on the alien Invasion. From there, they now work at a salvaged Alien Ship, from the looks of it seems to be one of the Heavy class ship of old. Earth is now subjugated and you are the leader of the resistance forces who fight against their rule. You, the Commander, must fight back against a new and sinister enemy know as ADVENT, an governemnt organization created by the Coalition between humans and the Alien Elders, while trying to stop a secret project that could be the end of mankind.
GAMEPLAY ASPECTS and thoughts on it:
> The RNG and POSITIONING
-Tactical based gameplay similar to the original game, but improved. More organized than the previous titles.
It requires not only strategic thinking to turn odds to your favor, but also a little bit of luck in a RNG dice roll. That said, the RNG is heavily influenced by how you are positioned and protected.
You will not hit every shot, and the aliens can hit you with some lucky shots, however both of you are governed by the same rules, with the veteran difficulty balancing the tip towards your favor with "Miss Streaks" and "Aim Assists" for your soldiers. At higher difficulties, those differences cease, you and the aliens obey the same odds.
A bad positioning effectively means your defeat, and a strong positioning can lead you to victory. Keep that in mind while playing and you will find yourself depending less on luck and more in how you place your troops. (It may happen the hilarious 95% chance miss, it's not frequent and quite rare, unless the game really decided to hate you all of a sudden).
> SKILLS and ABILITIES
-Abilities are important, as they can bless you with guaranteed hits you will definetly need in some situations. It can turn the tide of battles very quickly to your favor. That said, the enemy can do the very same things with their abilities should the circunstances present themselves. Two units close to each may result in a grenade flying towards you. Or one of the powerful abilities the aliens have may be used against you.
With that in mind you will understand that some aliens must be taken out first, or that will result in one of your troopers being dragged across the map or half of your squad poisoned.
Different Aliens mean different aproach and different strategies, learn your enemy in order to defeat them.
> CLASSES and PROGRESS
- There are effectively 4 default classes for your troops with 1 special class divided in two ability trees that give them different roles in combat, the abilities can be mixed, so you are not stuck with just one role or the other, and given the proper infrastructure, you can retrain them (although you cannot change their class)
- The Aliens do have different types of enemies with different abilities, however their upgrades are based around the progression know as "force level" and "Dark Events".
-> The force level effectively defines the type of alien you will face, as well as the upgrades towards aliens you already encounter. A common trooper will become and Advanced trooper as the time moves forward, and later in the game you will be facing Elite level troopers and more powerful Aliens.
-> Dark Events are strategic elements that rule over your campaign, they can last 1 to 2 months depending on the Event, or add points to their secret project. They can range from adding poison coated ammo to your enemies, or sent a UFO to hunt your SHIP.
>RESEARCH:
The research element is straight to the point, have a material, research it. Have a corpse, autopsy it. Have a thing, do this thing. You can improve your research time with more scientists.
>ENGINEERING:
Also straight to the point. You research a thing, you acquired a blueprint on that thing, you build that thing.
With the exception on the proving grounds, where takes time to construct an armor or make said blueprint. Experimental item blueprints give you a random item that can make a hell of a difference in your performance. Or building an more advanced armor that is not the default medium choice.
-TIP-
Research and Engineering can save you if you had your star squad wiped by a couple of bad decisions, however, losing missions over and over may result in campaign victory for the aliens, and you falling behind in force level category, where there's simply no way for you to face them anymore without you effectively turning a simple encounter into an epic struggle between untrained troops and powerful alien overlords.
Which most of the time will result in Death if you are not of the most experienced XCOM player.
That said, these elements make an realistic representation in technology gap, if you don't keep up with your enemy, you will get steam rolled across the battlefield. It also means that if you manage to get the Early advantage in boosting your crew Engineers and Scientist staff, you will effectively do the same thing to them, although it all comes down in how you manage your squad into battle. Once you get the hang of it, you will rarely lose a mission, maybe a soldier or two.
>STORYLINE MISSIONS and OBJECTIVES:
- There are a couple of missions that represent the Storyline progression, which are required to complete in order to reach the end and win the game. Some have the term of "catasthropical failure", which results in instant victory for the aliens should you lose it. Missions with that term allow you to restart it and try again, or restart the game with a new campaign. One of the two.
--------- In regards to DLC -----------
Alien Hunters:
- This DLC adds four new powerful itens and three new powerful aliens for you to face along your campaign. With a story element should you decide to have the complete.
-> Having the story mode selected you will have a mission that starts the scenario, the enemies will not appear until you decide to.
-> Not having the story mode selected results in the enemies appearing normaly in the campaign and the weapons appearing in the engineering section for you to build them.
Shen's last gift:
- This DLC adds a MEC to your squad. An early game useless unit but a late game monster with the technological improvements. Like the Alien Hunters, it does have an story element that allows you to start the DLC. If not selected, you will be able to build it as soon as you get the Proving grounds.
Anarchy's Children:
- A cosmetic DLC, it adds anarchy themed cosmetics to the game for you soldiers customization. The flavour is not for everyone and honestly, you can find better mods for your cosmetics. Although it has a cool piece here and there, it doesn't justify a DLC.
Resistance warrior pack:
- Another cosmetic DLC, that in it's size, doesn't justify a DLC. And for some reason is not included in the reinforcement pack.
------- Personal suggestion for developers --------
If you are planning on making a DLC for the game, i would suggest one where we could play as the Aliens in their Storyline, it seems that it has a room for expansion and will allow for a different perspective. It would introduce an different aspect to the game since the we would be playing on the Aliens Side. and will allow for some player to have a choice to subjugate humanity, or not, depending what the aliens are really thinking.
It seems like a silly suggestion but it has room for potential if done correctly.
------- Overall ---------
It's a game that is supposed to be Brutal and unforgiving on combat side, any early mistake can lead to a defeat. It does get easier over time as you progress, but even so, it's not for casual or newbies that can't learn from their mistakes. Although Veterans can have a very casual experience.
Overall.
8 / 10 for Gameplay. 7 / 10 for Strategy. 4 / 10 for DLC. 7 / 10 for Story.

Let me start off by stating that I have always tried to stand by my decision to support Bethesda's products I loved Morrowind, Oblivion, Fallout 3, Fallout: New Vegas, And Skyrim all to death. However there comes a time when I just cannot agree with what is being done by them.
Fallout 4 is a good game, just not a very good 'Fallout' game. Instead of deepening the RPG experience Bethesda has chosen to water the game down in favor of a broader audience, and to make it easier for all. Overall they made several improvements I would happily have used in previous titles, but they took major steps backwards as well. The story, depth, player interaction/choices, and focus on settlements instead of doing something productive has taken this game from what could be a masterpiece to an overall shameful display. Alongside this there are blatantly game breaking bugs that Bethesda could have fixed at any point, along with some overall weak DLC content that didn't add a ton - Except Nuka-World, Nuka-World was good.
Mods help Fallout 4 to be a very good experience, but if I mention mods I have to mention the Creation Club and what is more or less paid mods/Microtransactions with a different terminology. Bethesda's games have been known for having very active modding communities for a long time now, and they probably will for a long time to come but Bethesda also needs to acknowledge that the community at large wants nothing to do with paid mods or microtransactions in a single player game, especially when the mods they offer can be obtained for free on the PC platform. Unfortunately the creation club is the only solution for Playstation 4 users to get anything outside of what Bethesda hand-made, which is a real shame for them. Despite my sympathies to PS4 users, shoving paid mods down my throat wasn't the solution we or they needed. Modders do what they do best because they are passionate for it, not because there's a pay-check at the end, that's what game designers are for. Several big modding communities and projects have set up methods for donations to get to them as well, if people wanted to offer money there is always a method for it to happen.
Despite the laundry list of issues one could propose for Fallout 4, the core of the game isn't a bad one. A handful of mods to fix the gamebreaking issues, a few mods to make your time in Boston more interesting, and this is a good game. But my personal opinion on it will remain as not recommended so long as this Creation Club fiasco is breathing down our throats.
Thanks for taking the time to read this, I hope it helped someone.
